articles.body:
Última hora del Barcelona - Paris Basketball

¡¡¡Muuuy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a todos y todas a la duodécima jornada de la Euroliga !!! El Barcelona recibe al Paris Basketball para ampliar su espectacular racha de cinco victorias seguidas que han aupado al equipo de Aleksander Sekulic a la cuarta plaza , empatado con el grupo de líderes de la competición . Tras su heroica remontada en el OAKA , buscarán un nuevo triunfo contra un conjunto de la parte media baja de la tabla .

El conjunto azulgrana venció al Panathinaikos (74-76) tras un último cuarto espectacular (17-33), liderado por un Justin Robinson en ebullición, con 24 puntos. El Barcelona encadena cinco triunfos consecutivos que le ha hecho escalar hasta el liderato de la Euroliga . En medio de una dinámica que se eleva a nueve contando los de Liga Endesa , los de Sekulic sustentan estos resultados fuera de casa; en el Palau marchan 3-2 , dejándose ambos partidos contra equipos de la zona alta, como Zalgiris y Olympiacos .

Enfrente, un Paris Basketball que está decimocuarto con un balance negativo de 5-6, pero en un gran estado de forma con cuatro partidos ganados de manera consecutiva. De hecho, el club francés acumula tres de esas lejos de Francia , venciendo en las canchas de Dubai , Maccabi y Anadolu Efes, que se suma a la agónica victoria en casa ante Fenerbahce. Con el eléctrico Nadir Hifi al frente, el base galo se acompaña de otros jugadores como Ntilikina, Rhoden, Herrera o Faye , entre otros.

Desde las 20.30 horas , contaremos este partidazo de la mejor competición continental entre dos conjuntos alegres y muy ofensivos, como siempre, aquí en MARCA .

articles.title: Partizan Belgrado - Valencia Basket | Resumen, resultado y estadísticas del partido de la Euroliga
articles.summary: El Valencia, con su victoria, sigue líder de la Euroliga, igualado con el Olympiacos que ganó al Maccabi con un triple increíble de Vezenkov para forz
articles.body:
Hola, muy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a la Euroliga . Con todos ustedes... el líder de la Euroliga . El Valencia es el sorprendente primer clasificado sobre todo teniendo en cuenta que cambió la mayor parte de su plantilla en la pretemporada y ha logrado incluso un hito que el año pasado no pudo como es su mejor arranque histórico en la competición.

Los taronja visitan al Partizan de Joan Peñarroya para tratar de conservar una semana más el honor de encabezar la tabla. El equipo serbio, undécimo después de un gran arranque, vienen de ganar sus dos últimos partidos, ambos como locales, ante el Maccabi y el Kosner Baskonia . El Valencia , por su parte, ha logrado cuatro triunfos en sus últimos cinco partidos y su 4-1 de balance en partidos jugador lejos del Roig Arena le convierten en claro favorito para este choque.

En el Partizan se lo perderán Kevarius Hayes, Joffrey Lauvergne (baja indefinida), Ethan Thompson y Derek Willis . En el Valencia , de nuevo, serán baja Nikola Mirotic y Nate Reuvers , que ya llevan varias semanas de ausencia con el equipo.

El partido comenzará a las 20.45 y te lo vamos a contar con todod etalle en MARCA.com.

articles.title: El Valencia baja al barro para someter al Partizan y mantener el liderato
articles.standfirst: La defensa serbia dejó a los taronjas con 20,4 puntos menos de su media (96,4). Brooks (15), Taylor (15+5) y Shorts (12+6), subsanan el cortocircuito ofensivo de su equipo
articles.summary: La defensa serbia dejó a los taronjas con 20,4 puntos menos de su media (96,4). Brooks (15), Taylor (15+5) y Shorts (12+6), subsanan el cortocircuito ofensivo de su equipo
articles.body: El Valencia Basket tuvo que emplearse a fondo y mostrar su versión más terrenal para consolidar su liderato tras someter a un Partizan que le planteó muchas dificultades obturando con eficacia su prolífico ataque (64-76). El plan de los serbios casi les sale bien, pues dejaron a los taronjas con 20,4 puntos menos de su media habitual (96,4). Pero el equipo de Peñarroya no contaba con que su rival bajase al barro y demostrase que también sabe ganar cuando su maquinaria ofensiva es atorada. En el último cuarto fue Puerto con seis puntos seguidos quien abrió la brecha definitiva (54-65, min 36) para un Valencia sin Mirotic que sobrevivió a la formidable tenacidad ofensiva serbia con el talento de Brooks (15), Taylor (15+5), Shorts (12+6) y el propio Puerto (9), mientras Sako (11 rebotes) y Rivero (9+6) imponían sus tentáculos en la zona. El imparable Carlik Jones (21+2+5) estuvo demasiado solo en un Partizan que adoleció de argumentos para derrotar al líder. El Partizan salió centrado en apretar las clavijas en defensa para menguar el habitual caudal ofensivo del Valencia y lo logró durante el primer cuarto (13-16, min 10). Shorts y Taylor llevaron el peso de los taronjas junto al hiperactivo Cárdenas, que pagó su intensidad con una prematura segunda falta que le mandó al banquillo. Carlik Jones y Pajola daban la réplica para los serbios. En el segundo acto el Valencia igualó la intensidad defensiva de su aguerrido rival, aseguró el rebote, pudo por fin correr y logró liberarse de la camisa de fuerza del Partizan durante un par de minutos para abrir la primera brecha importante con triples de Brooks, Taylor y Osetkowski (19-29). Encajaron bien el golpe los serbios, que se revolvieron hasta situarse por delante con un parcial de 15-4 con triples de Marinkovic y Franks, la inspiración de Jekiri y una técnica a Xavi Albert (34-33). Un 2+1 de Shorts permitió a los taronjas llegar con ventaja al descanso (34-36, min 20). El resultado reforzó la fe del Partizan en su ímpetu para dificultar la habitual barra libre del Valencia y volvió a ponerlo en práctica con éxito en la reanudación. Los taronjas igualaron el envite defensivo y el resultado fue que hubo que esperar casi cinco minutos para ver la primera canasta en juego de la segunda parte. Puerto, con seis puntos, comando otro arreón de su equipo (41-48, min 28), pero Markovic, Jones y Stevens fabricaron un 10-4 para reducir a la mínima expresión la desventaja antes del último acto (51-52, min 30). Llegó entonces la embestida definitiva del Valencia, que con cuatro puntos de Brooks, cuatro de Taylor y un triple de Puerto puso la máxima (54-65, min 34). Los serbios se resistieron a claudicar con un 2+1 de Franks y una canasta de Marinkovic (59-65). Pero Brooks abrochó el triunfo con un triple a 1.17 del final (61-70). Vildoza contestó rápido con otro buscando el milagro, pero el Valencia no dejó ni un resquicio a la remontada y abrochó el triunfo con un 2+1 de Rivero y un triple postrero de Brooks para consolidar así su liderato en la Euroliga (64-76). 64 - Partizan (13+21+17+13): Jones (21), Marinkovic (10), Pajola (3), Franks (10) Jekiri (9) -cinco titular- Vildoza (3), Tanaskovic (2), Reeves (-), Stevens (6), Lakic (-) y Silva (-). 76 - Valencia Basket (16+20+16+24): TJ Shorts (12), Saint-Supéry (4), Taylor (15), Osetkowski (3), Sako (-) -cinco titular- Cárdenas (5), Moore (2), Corbalán (2), Brooks (12), Puerto (9), Gueye (-) y Rivero (9). Árbitros: Lottermoser (GER), Sukys (LTU) y Thepenier (FRA). Sin eliminados. Incidencias: partido correspondiente a la duodécima jornada de la fase regular de la Euroliga disputado en el Belgrado Arena ante cerca de quince mil espectadores.

articles.title: Novena derrota seguida del Kosner Baskonia, que ya es colista en solitario
articles.standfirst: Los vitorianos, que no conocen el triunfo en Euroliga con Perasovic, se condenan en un pésimo último cuarto (11-21)
articles.summary: Los vitorianos, que no conocen el triunfo en Euroliga con Perasovic, se condenan en un pésimo último cuarto (11-21)
articles.body: Hapoel Tel-Aviv rompió su mala racha en la Eurliga ante el Kosner Baskonia, al que superó en la recta final del partido por 82-85, después de ir por detrás la gran mayoría de los minutos pero mejorar en el último cuarto. Fue uno de los partidos más serios del equipo de Velimir Perasovic, que sigue sin conseguir el triunfo europeo, mientras que los hebreos recuperaron la senda de la victoria después de tres partidos perdidos de forma consecutiva. Kenan Kamenjas fue el más regular con 12 puntos y 12 rebotes, pero la conexión de Vasilije Micic con los interiores Oturu y Odiase fue fundamental para aguantar en el partido a los de Dimitris Itoudis. Dan Oturu y Kenan Kamenjas libraron su particular batalla inicial en un comienzo igualado, en el que comenzaron a entrar los jugadores exteriores de los dos equipos para darle más ritmo al choque. Tai Odiase castigó la pintura con seis puntos consecutivos, pero saltaron a la pista DJ Stewart y Chris Duarte para aportar alternativas ofensivas a un Baskonia que comenzó con ritmo y fluidez para alcanzar una renta de 8 puntos en un primer asalto que se cerró de tres en tres con un 33-26. Eliyah Bryant comenzó a generar el conjunto hebreo dio un salto importante en los primeros ataques del segundo periodo, en el que Chris Duarte seguía con el punto de mira alineado y con su cuarto triple mantuvo a raya a los de Dimitris Itoudis. A pesar de los once puntos de diferencia para los locales, el rebote ofensivo mantuvo en partido al conjunto israelí, que dio un pase adelante en defensa y propinó un parcial de 0-7 para dejar todo abierto de cara a la segunda parte, 48-44. El trabajo de Kenan Kamenjas en la pintura dio muchos réditos en ataque a los locales, que volvieron a abrir brecha con seis puntos del interior bosnio en los primeros compases del tercer acto. Respondieron Vasilje Micic y Dan Oturu para aguantar el arranque vitoriano y seguir de cerca al Baskonia, que sufría con el físico que imponía el equipo de Tel-Aviv, que dio la vuelta al marcador después 17 minutos. Los azulgranas reaccionaron con un 11-2, y ocho puntos de Rolands Smits, para recuperar el liderazgo en el electrónico, 71-64. Hapoel tuvo las ideas más claras en el comienzo del último cuarto y apretaron las tuercas con un 2-10, para recuperar el liderato en el peor momento ofensivo de Baskonia, que anotó dos puntos en cinco minutos. DJ Stewart mantuvo a flote a los vitorianos, que igualaron las fuerzas cuando Kobi Simmons cometía una polémica quinta falta. Micic encontró a Tai Odiase en los últimos ataques y Baskonia no pudo anotar para enviar a la prórroga un partido que acabó 82-85. 82 - Baskonia (33+15+23+11): Kobi Simmons (7), A.J. Lawson (8), Rodions Kurucs (2), Clement Frisch (9) y Kenan Kamenjas (12) -cinco inicial-, D.J. Árbitros: Mehdi Difallah (Francia), Piotr Pastusiak (Polonia) y Stefan Calic (Serbia). Eliminaron a Simmons por faltas personales. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la jornada 12 de la Euroliga, disputado en el Buesa Arena de Vitoria ante 2.186 espectadores. articles.title: Detroit Pistons vs. San Antonio Spurs Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs' 12-game win streak has come to an end.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs' 12-game win streak has come to an end.

Despite playing on the road without two starters and two key reserves, the Detroit Pistons pulled off the 105-93 victory Tuesday night. Cade Cunningham (27 points, six assists), Ausar Thompson (14 points, 12 assists) and Daniss Jenkins (25 points, five assists) were all spectacular. Detroit's defense writ large was hellfire.

Victor Wembanyama racked up a ho-hum 25 points, 18 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. San Antonio lost this one with him on the bench. It was outscored by 18 points in the minutes he didn't play.

Dylan Harper finished with 20 points but left the game late in the fourth quarter after suffering what appeared to be a groin injury. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle combined for just 16 points, and Julian Champagnie was held scoreless in the second half after dropping 14 points in the first two frames.

Scroll below to check out all the most important updates, highlights, takeaways and analysis from this clash of contenders.

Ausar Thompson Earned a Piece of Pistons History

Dylan Harper's Favorite Player is Who?!?

This throwback is canon because I said so. Nobody show it to Wemby.

Victor Wembanyama Sounds Off on the Spurs' Offensive Struggles

"Our mistakes looked kind of obvious. I'm not going to expand on them."

Thank you for this glorious peak behind the curtain, Wemby. Next time, though, consider being more vague. You don't want to give away too many of your team's closed-door secrets.

Never mind the 25 points and five assists Jenkins dropped tonight. He's averaging around 14 points and 4.5 assists per game for the season—while drilling more than 42 percent of his triples.

Impressive still, Jenkins is hitting 37.5 percent of his pull-up threes. That's a demonstrative upgrade from the 23.8 percent clip he posted last season. When he's hitting these shots, it changes the geometry of the floor while elevating the ceiling of Detroit's offense.

The Calls for Tarris Reed to Play are Getting Louder

The Spurs are allowing nearly 120 points per 100 possessions without Wemby on the floor this season. Last year, they surrendered 113.7. That is a huge difference.

Color me skeptical that a rookie big man will solve it. At this point, though, it wouldn't hurt to try.

Damn, Cade! Cool it with these hot takes before you get burned.

The Pistons are REALLY Vibing Themselves After That Win

Did anyone else have to Google "YKTPWA" to find out it stood for "You know the Pistons won again" or is that just me?

Victor Wembanyama Comments on Dylan Harper Injury

All the usual prisoner-of-the-moment caveats apply, but these comments on Dylan Harper's injury feel rather ominous.

Cross your fingers that your resident alarmist (me) is wrong.

JB Bickerstaff Applauds Ausar Thompson's Playmaking

Twelve assists is a new career high for Ausar Thompson. He is now averaging 5.7 dimes per game on the season.

More importantly, Thompson has started cutting down on the turnovers. Though he's committed one on over 20 percent of his possessions overall, he has 28 assists against seven turnovers over the past three games.

Has Ausar Thompson Entered the All-Star Conversation?

Anytime you find yourself saying something to the effect of "If so-and-so keeps playing how he's played the last three games," the answer to the question that follows is probably no.

Still, if Thompson turns his current offensive impact into a new normal, then we can definitely have the discussion. But let's give it a minute.

This Cade Cunningham Postgame Quote is Tuff

Just to recap: No Jalen Duren. No Duncan Robinson. No Ron Holland II. No Isaiah Joe.

The Pistons won by 12, on the road, against the NBA's best team anyway.

Mitch Johnson Addresses the No-Wemby Minutes

The Spurs were a minus-18 without Wemby tonight and are now a minus-95 in 293 minutes without him for the season.

For reference, San Antonio was outscored last season by a total of one point through 2,080 minutes without Wemby on the court.

This comes as no surprise. The game just ended, and Harper limped off the court inside a minute to play.

Based on his reaction, this doesn't feel like an injury that'll just go away by tomorrow. And if that's the case, the Spurs will need Stephon Castle and De'Aaron Fox to take up more of the offensive scoring load than they did tonight.

The Spurs are Supposed to be Better Than This

De'Aaron Fox was particularly bad when looking at the supporting cast. His defense was fine for extended pockets, but the Spurs need him to be more aggressive when the half-court offense is going through the motions.

This holds especially true when Wemby is off the floor. Fox attempted just five shots in his minutes without the big man.

On the road, with two starters and two key reserves sidelined, the Pistons pulled off a big-time victory to end the Spurs' 12-game winning streak.

Credit Detroit's defense for keeping San Antonio's offense in the mud after the first quarter. The Spurs scored just 39 points in the second half and averaged just 0.65 points per play in the half-court over the final three frames.

Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins and Ausar Thompson were all big time. The non-Wemby minutes crushed San Antonio (minus-18). So, too, did the the lack of consistent secondary offense.

Dylan Harper dropped 20 points but was quiet for much of the game. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle combined for just 16 points. Julian Champagnie went off for 14 points in the first half, then was scoreless in the second half.

Dylan Harper is Being Helped to the Locker Room

Score: Pistons 103, Spurs 93 | 42.1 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter

This speaks to how comfortably the Spurs have been winning. On some level, though, it also seems like an acknowledgement the four-guard alignment isn't actually their best lineup. (Yes, I know what the numbers say.)

Score: Pistons 93, Spurs 87 | 3:06 remaining in the fourth quarter

The Spurs Might Need to Rethink Their Rotation

Look, you can't expect the Spurs to dominate the minutes without Wemby. But they are a minus-18 with Luke Kornet on the floor tonight. That's a problem.

Maybe Tobias Harris solves it by juicing the offense. If his return doesn't move the needle, the Spurs may need to consider dusting off the Tarris Reed Jr. or making a trade.

Score: Pistons 92, Spurs 84 | 3:40 remaining in the fourth quarter

Also of note: The Spurs have made just 10 shots in the second half, including only two in the fourth quarter.

Score: Pistons 88, Spurs 79 | 6:01 remaining in the fourth quarter

All of San Antonio is Holding Its Breath

On the bright side, Wemby seems to be fine. On the not-so-bright-side, he's currently off the floor with the Spurs trailing by double digits.

Score: Pistons 86, Spurs 75 | 7:43 remaining in the fourth quarter

The Pistons having the two best guards of this game is kinda, sorta, definitely a problem for the Spurs.

Javonte dunked so hard he nearly shattered his entire body. Eleven-out-of-10 stuff. No notes.

In related news, the Pistons are taking a six-point lead into the fourth quarter. The Spurs may need Wemby to play the rest of the way if they want to win.

Score: Pistons 78, Spurs 72 | End of the third quarter

Here is the Pistons' scoring breakdown in the paint, courtesy of PrimeStats.net :

With Wemby on the floor: 13-of-23 (11-of-13 at the rim)

Without Wemby on the floor: 10-of-14 (8-of-10 at the rim)

Basically, the Pistons have been getting into the paint regardless of whether Wemby's on the court. That's impressive.

The Spurs have been outscored by 17 points (32-15) with Wemby on the bench tonight. These minutes without him could literally determine the game.

Score: Pistons 70, Spurs 66 | 3:21 remaining in the third quarter

After having just five turnovers in the first half, the Pistons have committed three of them through the first four-and-a-half minutes of the third. The Spurs are now up by one.

Score: Spurs 62, Pistons 61 | 7:38 remaining in the third quarter

The Wemby self-oop looks, somehow, even more ridiculous from this angle.

Thompson went for 10 points and two assists in the second quarter alone. The energy he brought was palpable, and he gave the Pistons another ball-handler to use in lieu of Cade.

Cade Cunningham Gave the Pistons Their First Lead of the Game

Cade Cunningham dropped 11 points and three assists on a perfect 5-of-5 shooting inside the arc to spearhead a 29-21 second quarter for the Pistons.

Detroit did all of its damage with Wembanyama off the floor. Without him in the game, the offense was able to live in the paint. Having Ausar Thompson to run the floor and handle the ball helped, too. He has 10 points and four assists at the half.

At one point, the Spurs were dominating the paint battle. The Pistons are now a plus-eight there.

De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle, meanwhile, have combined for just 16 points between them. San Antonio will need someone other than Wemby and Julian Champagnie to score in the final two frames.

Cade Cunningham Through a Half-Court Bounce Pass

Hear me out: Cade Cunningham is good at basketball.

My guy isn't even looking anywhere near the basket.

Kevin Huerter is a Lob Threat, Apparently

Ausar Thompson is Stabilizing the Pistons

After sitting most of the first following two early fouls, Ausar Thompson has given the Pistons a ton of energy on the break and another ball-handling access point for the offense. Cade Cunningham is spending a touch more time away from the ball, and the Pistons have tied it up.

Score: Spurs 47, Pistons 45 | 4:33 remaining in the second quarter

So basically, Victor Wembanyama is going to win MVP? Got it.

Score: Spurs 47, Pistons 39 | 6:42 remaining in the second quarter

Off the top of my head, Dylan Harper seems to have Kyrie Irving- and Stephen Curry-tier footwork in his arsenal.

De'Aaron Fox with the Coolest Basket Interference of All Time

We get it, De'Aaron. You're strong enough to do at least one pull-up.

Julian Champagnie Sends Kevin Huerter Flying

Julian Champagnie is riding the wave of this first quarter highlight into the second. He is up to 14 points on 4-of-5 from three.

For reference, the Pistons' starters have totaled 16 points.

Score: Spurs 40, Pistons 26 | 10:09 remaining in the second quarter

This was simultaneously impressive and too easy. The Spurs' defense put up very little resistance after the initial press.

The Pistons are NOT Happy with Wemby's Ghost Foul

Detroit was called for tripping Wembanyama on the inbounds at the buzzer. The replay seemed to show he tripped over his own two feet, but the call stood. he made both free throws, which extended San Antonio's lead to seven.

San Antonio Takes a 7-Point Lead into the Second Quarter

Both teams scored 18 points in the paint during the first 12 minutes. Both had eight assists. Both shot under 30 percent from three. San Antonio made an additional triple and has more free throws and points in transition. Otherwise, the margins are slim.

Julian Champagnie leads all scorers with 11 points. Just as it should be.

Score: Spurs 33, Pistons 26 | End of the first quarter

They are "First quarter minutes for Chaz Lanier and Elijah Harkless" thin.

Victor Wembanyama Won't Stop Passing to Himself

For those keeping score at home, Wemby has now tossed two assists to himself. And we're still in the first quarter.

Double-digit leads are not what they used to be. Still, this is incredible.

Score: Spurs 24, Pistons 16 | 3:51 remaining in the first quarter

Ausar Thompson is Already in Foul Trouble

This is not what the shorthanded Pistons needed. They have already given up three offensive rebounds and are getting carved up near the paint.

Navigating the rest of the first quarter without Ausar Thompson will be a real test.

Victor Wembanyama Completes the Self-Oop

Wemby should get an assist and two points for this.

San Antonio has four buckets in the early going including the above one that highlights the synergy between Victor Wembanyama and Devin Vassell. We also have a Wemby pass-to-himself hoop in the bag, because of course.

Score: Spurs 8, Pistons 4 | 8:54 remaining in the first quarter

Winning 77 percent of your games for more than an entire season is actually bananas.

It has been refreshing to see Kevin Huerter recapture some of the magic from his "Light The Beam!" Sacramento Kings days.

Just in case you haven't heard this lineup is faring, the Spurs are outscoring opponents by 36.9 points per 100 possessions with their starters on the floor. Call me crazy, but that seems pretty good—particularly when they're only shooting 33 percent from downtown as a unit.

This is the starting five Detroit has been running, but with Kevin Huerter subbed in for Duncan Robinson.

In case you're wondering, the Pistons have played 17 minutes with this lineup on the year. So, they'll be getting some valuable data collection on its viability tonight.

The Pistons are Dealing with a Ton of Injuries

Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Isaiah Joe (hip) have already missed most of the season. Detroit now adds Duncan Robinson (quad strain) and Ron Holland II (knee) to its list of bang-ups.

Duren remains the biggest loss of all, but both Joe and Robinson are critical to the Pistons' half-court spacing. Going up against San Antonio's defense without them puts a ton of pressure of Kevin Huerter and Duncan Robinson.

Mitch Johnson Gives a Tobias Harris Update

Tobias Harris has yet to play this season while recovering from a left calf strain. The Spurs are doing perfectly fine without him, but the sooner they can see how his genre of scoring and physicality fits into their rotation, the better off they'll be.

Of note: Do not expect him to start upon return. Devin Vassell isn't crushing it from deep, but his three-point volume better leverages San Antonio's trio of point guards.

articles.title: Valencia aguanta como líder de la Euroliga: así está la clasificación
articles.standfirst: Sólo dos equipos, taronjas y Olympiacos, han llegado a nueve victorias en 12 jornadas
articles.summary: Sólo dos equipos, taronjas y Olympiacos, han llegado a nueve victorias en 12 jornadas
articles.body: La jornada arrancaba con cuatro equipos igualados en su balance con 8-3. Ahora sólo quedan dos. El Valencia y el Olympiacos ganaron sus partidos y se quedan con 9-3, con el Valencia liderando por segunda semana consecutiva por primera vez en la historia. Los de Xavi Albert ganaron en un partido embarrado al Partizan en Belgrado, demostrando que también pueden ganar cuando no pueden correr y el baloncesto no es tan espectacular. Su liderato, lejos de ser casual, se fundamenta en la solidez de su plantilla. El Olympiacos, por su parte ganó al Maccabi con un triple milagroso de Vezenkov desde su campo para forzar la prórroga y de Corey Joseph, al final del tiempo extra para ganar el partido. Valencia y Olympiacos se quedan solos por las derrotas del Panathinaikos y del Barça. Los griegos sufren su tercera derrota en los últimos cuatro partidos y están sumidos en una pequeña crisis de resultados. El Barça cerró su racha de cinco victorias seguidas en la Euroliga perdiendo en el último segundo con canasta de Hifi para dar el triunfo a París. Entre los resultados de la jornada, a falta del partido del Real Madrid ante el Besiktas, destaca el 117-114 del Zalgiris ante el Bayern con 32 puntos de Carsen Edwards. El Kosner Baskonia sigue colista con un horrible 1-12 de parcial. El Madrid, si gana este jueves, dará caza a varios equipos con ocho triunfos, entre los que están el Barça y el Panathnaikos.

articles.title: LSU adds All-American RJ Luis Jr. to basketball roster after court battle with SEC over his NBA contracts
articles.summary: Luis was the Big East Player of the Year and a consensus All-American at St. John's who projects to make an immediate impact for LSU.
articles.body:
LSU added former Big East Player of the Year RJ Luis Jr. to its basketball roster Tuesday, a day after SEC attorneys reportedly informed LSU that it would not seek to punish the program for playing him.

Luis and LSU had been embroiled in a legal battle with the SEC over his eligibility due to his signing of a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz after going unselected in the 2025 NBA Draft out of St. John's. The Jazz traded Luis to the Celtics, and Luis played in three preseason games for Boston in 2025.

Luis never played in a regular-season NBA game, and he and LSU contended that he was eligible to return to college to play for the Tigers. A Louisiana court ultimately agreed.

Baton Rouge judge repeatedly ruled in favor of LSU, athletes

Luis was granted multiple temporary injunctions, and Baton Rouge-based Judge William Jorden of Louisiana's 19th Judicial District issued a preliminary injunction on Friday stating that the SEC and NCAA could not legally penalize LSU for adding Luis to its roster.

Luis was listed on LSU's roster Tuesday, wearing No. 12 , and LSU system president Wade Rousse issued a statement confirming the roster move:

"LSU is committed to compliance with the NCAA and SEC rules, but it is equally committed to obeying the orders of Louisiana's courts. … "LSU is a member institution that will act in accordance with that order. The Conference has confirmed that it will do the same and has stated in writing that it 'will abide by the terms of the preliminary injunction while it remains in place and will not impose penalties or fines on LSU if it places Mr. Luis on its men's basketball roster."

"LSU is committed to compliance with the NCAA and SEC rules, but it is equally committed to obeying the orders of Louisiana's courts. …

"LSU is a member institution that will act in accordance with that order. The Conference has confirmed that it will do the same and has stated in writing that it 'will abide by the terms of the preliminary injunction while it remains in place and will not impose penalties or fines on LSU if it places Mr. Luis on its men's basketball roster."

The SEC responded with a statement calling the decision by LSU "deeply concerning" and "disappointing."

"LSU's decision today to rely on its own interpretation of the court's order to justify its actions is inconsistent with the expectations and responsibilities of membership in the Southeastern Conference," the unsigned statement reads. "This is a deeply concerning and disappointing development. The conference will continue to uphold and defend the standards and policies established by its member universities."

LSU's football eligibility saga with Lane Kiffin

Jorden is the same judge who granted more than 40 former NCAA athletes from the 2022 recruiting class a fifth year of eligibility in conflict with an NCAA ruling restricting them. That cleared the path for Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris and Jack Pyburn to join LSU's football roster in the preseason despite having been rostered in NFL training camps earlier in the summer.

The SEC responded to that ruling by considering punishing LSU for signing players who had signed pro contracts via game boycotts or even expulsion from the league .

Amid the uncertainty, LSU football ultimately did not include the players in question on the football roster . But Luis is now on LSU's basketball roster after being recruited by first-year head coach Will Wade.

Luis, 23, is a 6-foot-7 wing. He previously played one season at UMass and two at St. John's. As a junior at St. John's in 2024-25, Luis averaged 18.2 points, 7.2 rebounds, 2 assists and 1.4 steals per game while shooting 33.6% from 3.

The effort earned Luis the Big East Player of the Year award and consensus second-team All-America honors. He projects as an immediate impact player for a 4-0 LSU team that entered the AP poll at No. 25 this week.

articles.title: Stephen Curry opens up on retirement after signing $116 million Warriors extension, admits it could be his ‘last’ NBA contract
articles.summary: Stephen Curry has admitted that his latest contract with the Golden State Warriors could be one of the final deals of his NBA career.
articles.body: Stephen Curry has admitted that his latest contract with the Golden State Warriors could be one of the final deals of his NBA career. The four-time NBA champion recently signed a two-year, $116 million extension with the franchise, giving him a clearer picture of how much longer he could continue playing. However, the 38-year-old has not ruled out extending his career beyond the agreement. Curry acknowledged that he had already considered retirement while discussing his new deal, but also suggested that he might surprise himself by choosing to play for longer.The Warriors star’s comments come after months of questions about his future in Golden State. His contract situation had become an important talking point during the offseason, particularly after the franchise explored opportunities to bring another major name into the team.Stephen Curry admits $116 million Warriors extension could be his final NBA contractCurry opened up about his future after agreeing to the new deal with Golden State. The veteran guard admitted that he had expected the agreement to be among the final contracts he would sign during his playing career.“I assumed that it would probably be one of, if not the last, contracts I signed. I’m not afraid to say it. But maybe I’ll surprise myself and want to keep going.”His comments offer a glimpse into how the 38-year-old is thinking about the final stage of his basketball career. While he understands that retirement is getting closer, he has not made a final decision about when he wants to leave the game.The two-year, $116 million agreement also includes a player option for its final year. Curry accepted a pay cut as part of the deal, which came after the Warriors spent much of the offseason looking at ways to strengthen their roster.Golden State had been linked with several big names, including Giannis Antetokounmpo and LeBron James, but neither move materialised. Curry’s extension eventually gave the franchise greater certainty about the future of its most important player.Could Stephen Curry retire after the 2028-29 NBA season?Curry’s new contract is scheduled to expire after the 2028-29 season. If he completes the agreement, it would take him through his 20th season in the NBA, having spent his entire professional career with the Warriors.That would also put him within reach of a rare milestone. Only seven players in NBA history have played more than 20 seasons. Curry could become the eighth if he decides to continue beyond his current contract.His teammate Al Horford, who is already a 20-year NBA veteran, could reach that mark before him.Curry has already secured his place among the league’s greatest shooters. He holds the NBA all-time records for three-pointers made and attempted, as well as career free-throw percentage.The Warriors guard has also built a career that has made him one of the defining players of his generation. However, his latest comments suggest that he is aware his time on the court will not last forever.For now, there is no confirmed retirement date. Curry remains open to continuing beyond his latest contract, leaving the possibility of another season or even another deal on the table. Whether he chooses to do so will depend on how he feels when the 2028-29 season approaches.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New lawsuit alleges AI app 'Bron' used LeBron James’ tattoos, voice and jersey to promote sports-betting tool
articles.summary: LeBron James alleges an AI sports-betting app called "Bron" faked his endorsement, with its ad viewed about 1 million times before it was taken down.
articles.body: LeBron James filed a lawsuit Tuesday against the developers of an AI sports-betting app, accusing the company of violating his publicity rights and trademarks by branding the product "Bron" and using AI-generated images of him in marketing materials. The lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court in New York, claims the developers used James’ name, likeness and nickname without permission to promote an otherwise unknown product. James’ attorneys described the alleged conduct as "a willful, bad-faith tactic" designed to capitalize on the 76ers star’s fame. The complaint asks the court to bar the developers from using James’ name, surrender any resulting profits and pay damages, including the fair-market value of its alleged use and punitive damages. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Defendants did not care that they had engaged in illegal conduct to gain notoriety for their previously unknown app," the lawsuit read. "They intentionally created the false impression that Mr. James endorsed and was affiliated with their Bron App, in an effort to drive downloads and paid subscriptions." PlayVision Inc., the California-based developer of the app, was launched in 2025 by CEO Anish Gupta and CTO Marc Zoghby with backing from startup accelerator Y Combinator. The company developed a platform that uses artificial intelligence to analyze game and practice footage for sports teams and fans. LEBRON JAMES SENDS CEASE AND DESIST TO 'BRON AI' SPORTS BETTING APP OVER UNAUTHORIZED LIKENESS PlayVision launched the "Bron" app this year, saying it does not accept wagers directly but charges a subscription fee for features such as bet tracking and odds comparisons. A marketing campaign this month depicted a person resembling James, complete with similar tattoos, voice and No. 23 jersey, using the app in a locker room. Messages sent by OutKick through the app’s website seeking comment were not immediately returned Tuesday. A spokesperson for James previously confirmed that his lawyers sent the company a cease-and-desist letter. PlayVision removed the ad, but not before it was reposted and viewed roughly 1 million times, according to the lawsuit. "I’m sure the intent here was for us to send a cease and desist in order to make it a story," James' longtime media advisor Adam Mendelsohn told Front Office Sports. "You would prefer not to respond but you don’t have a choice in a situation like this. It’s not the first time and it won’t be the last. For what it’s worth, these gimmicks never work because people see through it." LEBRON JAMES SAYS 'MY FAMILY IS SAFE' AFTER MAN CAUGHT ON GROUNDS OF HIS LOS ANGELES HOME Gupta responded to the attorneys’ demand on social media by writing that the app would get a new name, but no new name had been adopted by the time the lawsuit was filed, leading James’ legal team to suggest the company was milking the controversy for attention. Gupta wrote on social media this week that the new name will be announced Wednesday. The lawsuit notes that James typically commands tens of millions of dollars for such endorsement deals, and that he already has an exclusive deal with the prediction market platform Polymarket. It alleges that the app’s marketing was especially harmful in part because it showed the AI-generated James scrolling through bets involving NBA players. Through 15 games of the 2026-27 season, Philadelphia’s 12 wins lead the Eastern Conference. James’ former team also has 12 wins and is tied with the San Antonio Spurs atop the Western Conference. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Pistons overcome highlight-reel Victor Wembanyama to stun Spurs, snap San Antonio's 12-game win streak
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama made highlights, and the San Antonio Spurs took early control in Tuesday's showdown with the Detroit Pistons. But when Wembanyama left the...
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama made highlights , and the San Antonio Spurs took early control in Tuesday's showdown with the Detroit Pistons.

But when Wembanyama left the floor, the Pistons feasted. And they rallied from a 33-24 first-quarter hole behind a strong defensive effort for a 105-93 statement win over the Spurs in San Antonio.

The win snapped a 12-game win streak for the now 12-3 Spurs, who hadn't previously lost since dropping their first two games of the season. And a Pistons team that flamed out in the playoffs after posting the best record in the East last season now has a signature win of the new campaign to improve to 9-4.

Cade Cunningham has been among the NBA's hottest players with 52 and 33 points in consecutive games before Tuesday. He led the way again Tuesday night with 27 points, 5 rebounds and 6 assists.

While his teammates repeatedly attacked the rim when Wembanyama was on the bench, Cunningham took it right at the Spurs MVP candidate with a highlight-reel attack and dunk to end the first quarter.

Wembanyama went to the bench in the second quarter with the Spurs holding a 42-34 lead. When he returned, the Pistons had cut their deficit to 47-46 as shots at the bucket went repeatedly unchallenged.

The Pistons then took control with a 23-18 third quarter advantage as San Antonio's shooting went cold. The Spurs played from behind for the entirety of the fourth quarter and weren't able to retake the lead.

When it was done, a Pistons team playing without injured center Jalen Duren (hamstring) won the battle inside with a 60-44 advantage in points in the paint. Ausar Thompson was a force all over the court with 14 points, 12 assists, 9 rebounds and 5 steals while shooting 7 of 13 from the floor.

Daniss Jenkins provided a boost from the perimeter with 25 points while shooting 3 of 7 from 3. The Pistons shot 49.5% from the field while holding the Spurs to a 41.6% clip and a 9-of-40 (22.5%) effort from 3.

Wemby dominant inside, but struggles from deep

Wembanyama was a force inside and put on a show with a pair of first-quarter dunks that came off passes from himself off the backboard.

He finished the game with 23 points and 18 rebounds. But he struggled more than any of his teammates from long range with a 1-of-8 effort from 3.

Dylan Harper added 20 points, 4 rebounds and 2 assists on 8-of-14 shooting from the field. But he missed all four of his 3s and left late with what appeared to be a groin injury.

With the game in the final minute, Harper slipped and did a split as he tried to plant his right foot. He remained down on the ground in pain and clutched his groin as the Pistons played 5-on-4 on the other side of the court.

The precise nature and severity of his injury wasn't initially clear, but he needed help getting up before limping to the locker room on his own before the game's conclusion.

Harper's thrived since joining San Antonio's starting lineup in his second NBA season with averages of 18.3 points, 5.5 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game. An extended absence would be a difficult blow for the Spurs on top of Tuesday's loss.

The Spurs are left to regroup from a thorough defeat on their home court and a potentially significant injury that abruptly snapped the high of a 12-game win streak. They have upcoming games against the Clippers, Pelicans and Kings before a difficult three-game stretch against the Trail Blazers, Lakers and Celtics.

The Pistons will remain on the road Wednesday against the Pelicans before facing the Raptors and Hawks over the weekend.

articles.title: Spurs guard Dylan Harper slips on court late in loss to Pistons, limps off with apparent groin injury
articles.summary: Dylan Harper slipped on a wet spot on Tuesday night, and his legs went opposite ways as he awkwardly fell to the court.
articles.body:
The court at the Frost Bank Center got Dylan Harper on Tuesday night.

With about a minute left in the San Antonio Spurs' 105-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons , Harper suddenly went down on the wing right as Stephon Castle was passing him the ball. While it looked like Harper was maybe hit in real time, a closer look revealed that he just slipped on the court and his legs went opposite ways.

Harper was rolling around on the court holding his groin, clearly in a lot of pain, as play continued the other direction. He eventually stood up and walked back to the locker room after play stopped and the athletic training staff came out, but Harper looked very uncomfortable moving as he worked his way into the tunnel.

"It just looked like he slipped, obviously, so hoping for the best, but don't know anything yet," Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said, via the San Antonio Express-News' Tom Orsborn .

Harper did not return to the game. He finished with 20 points and four rebounds while shooting 8 of 14 from the field in the loss, which was the Spurs' third of the season and snapped their 12-game win streak.

Harper entered Tuesday's contest averaging 18.3 points, 5.5 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game this season, all of which are improvements from his rookie campaign. The Spurs selected Harper with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft out of Rutgers.

The Pistons rallied in the second half Tuesday night to secure the 12-point win in San Antonio. They ended the contest on a 10-3 burst and held the Spurs scoreless in the final 90 seconds.

Cade Cunningham led the way with 27 points in the win, which pushed the Pistons to 9-4 on the season. Daniss Jenkins added 25 points, and Ausar Thompson finished just shy of a triple-double with 14 points, 12 assists, 9 rebounds.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 25 points and 18 rebounds. He had two ridiculous self-alley-oop dunks in the first quarter. Devin Vassell added 12 points, and Castle finished with 10 points and seven assists.

Though it's unclear how long Harper may be sidelined because of the injury, losing him for any significant stretch will make things much more difficult for the Spurs as they try to remain at the top of the Western Conference standings.

articles.title: No. 14 Tennessee shuts down No. 2 Michigan State, holds Jeremy Fears without a field goal in upset win
articles.summary: Michigan State only made nine field goals on Tuesday night, its fewest output over the past 30 seasons.
articles.body:
It took a complete defensive clinic — and a bucket-less outing from Jeremy Fears Jr. — for the Volunteers to pull off the upset win on Tuesday night in Knoxville.

No. 14 Tennessee shut down No. 2 Michigan State to grab a 61-46 win over the Spartans in what was one of the first great upsets of the new college basketball season. The Vols limited Michigan State to just nine field goals throughout the contest, which marked the program's fewest made field goals in a single game over the past 30 seasons.

Fears, a preseason All-American who was fresh off a stellar win over then-No. 2 Duke last week, didn't make a single one of those field goals. He finished with 16 points, all of which came from the free-throw line, and went 0-of-3 from the field.

The win marked the 48th consecutive home nonconference victory for the Volunteers, and their seventh straight home win over teams ranked in the top five. They are now 4-0.

Tennessee surged ahead at the end of the first half, thanks in part to an 11-0 burst that put the Vols out in front for the first time all night. That didn't slow down after halftime. They opened the second half on a 10-0 run, capped by a huge Juke Harris 3-pointer that forced a Tom Izzo timeout. At that point, with an extended 21-2 run working, the Volunteers had taken a 12-point lead.

Miles Rubin came out of that break with a dunk of his own. In total, Michigan State went more than 10 minutes without making a field goal.

Michigan State slowly crawled back into the contest, and held Tennessee scoreless for almost six minutes in the second half to cut the deficit to just two possessions.

But, as it turns out, it's incredibly hard to win a game without making a field goal. The Spartans made only three in the second half, the last of which came in the form of a Cam Ward layup with 4:31 left in the second half. They managed just three points the rest of the way as Tennessee pulled away for good to grab the 15-point win.

The Spartans finished shooting 9 of 50 from the field in the loss. Ward added 12 points and five rebounds off the bench while making four of those field goals himself. He and Fears were the only two Spartans to hit double figures. Jasiah Jervis, who took the most shots for Michigan State, was 0 for 10 from the floor.

Rubin finished with 14 points and eight rebounds for the Volunteers. DeWayne Brown added 14 points and seven rebounds. They shot 46% from the field. Tennessee head coach Rick Barnes has now beaten top-five teams 30 times in his career, which is the fourth-most in Associated Press poll history. Tennessee's 7-0 record against top-five teams in the Rick Barnes era is the best mark in the country over that span.

While Tennessee may not be an offensive juggernaut in the SEC this season, its defense is for real. The Volunteers proved they can shut down one of the best guards in the nation Tuesday night, a feat that should carry them through the early stretch of the season and set them up nicely come conference play.

articles.title: Fever’s Front Office Search Takes Major Turn as NBA Executives Emerge

articles.body:
The Indiana Fever are moving closer to finding their next basketball executive, and their search has drawn three candidates with extensive NBA experience.

Boston Celtics vice president Allison Feaster, Sacramento Kings vice president Phil Jabour and former Dallas Mavericks executive Matt Riccardi have emerged as strong candidates for the position, according to Annie Costabile and Sam Amick of The Athletic , who first reported the development Tuesday, Nov. 17.

ESPN's Alexa Philippou and Shams Charania subsequently reported that Indiana is working through a group of finalists, with a hire expected within the next month.

Philippou also clarified that the Fever intend to hire one basketball operations executive rather than separate replacements for former team president Kelly Krauskopf and former general manager Amber Cox.

The search comes at a critical point for Indiana, which must address major roster decisions surrounding Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell.

The development comes nearly four weeks after the Fever parted ways with two of their highest-ranking executives.

Fever Identify Three Leading Front Office Candidates

Feaster brings a combination of playing experience and NBA front office leadership.

A former WNBA player, she currently serves as Boston's vice president of team operations and organizational growth. She joined the Celtics in 2019 after an accomplished professional playing career.

Her work has focused on player development, organizational culture and relationships throughout the basketball operation.

The Kings executive has worked extensively in scouting, player evaluation and roster construction. Before joining Sacramento, he held a scouting leadership position with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Riccardi, meanwhile, previously served as an assistant general manager with the Mavericks.

He also spent more than a decade with the Brooklyn Nets organization, including a stint running their G League affiliate.

Following Nico Harrison's dismissal in Dallas in November 2025, Riccardi and Michael Finley briefly shared interim general manager responsibilities.

All three candidates bring NBA experience, although Indiana has not announced a finalist or identified a preferred choice.

Fever Planning One Hire After Major Leadership Shake-Up

The Fever's search began after team president Kelly Krauskopf stepped down Oct. 23.

General manager and chief operating officer Amber Cox departed later that day, leaving Indiana with significant vacancies in basketball leadership.

However, Philippou clarified that the Fever intend to hire one basketball executive rather than separate replacements for Krauskopf and Cox.

The incoming executive will inherit a franchise with championship expectations and several consequential personnel decisions approaching.

Krauskopf helped build the Fever from their inception and guided the franchise through its first WNBA championship in 2012.

Cox, meanwhile, oversaw basketball operations during a period of heightened attention surrounding the team's young core.

Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell Await Fever's Next Move

The timing of Indiana's search adds urgency to the decision.

Caitlin Clark remains the centerpiece of the franchise, while Kelsey Mitchell enters another important offseason following a career-best 2026 campaign.

Mitchell's upcoming free agency presents an immediate challenge for whoever takes charge.

The four-time All-Star has established herself as one of the WNBA's premier scorers, making her future a central question in Indiana's plans.

The next executive must also evaluate the roster around Clark and Mitchell while working with coach Stephanie White to establish a sustainable championship contender.

Indiana's leadership changes have created uncertainty. Tuesday's report, however, suggests the search is entering its final stages.

With several NBA-connected candidates under consideration and a decision expected within weeks, the Fever could soon have the person responsible for guiding their next chapter.

articles.title: Knicks coach Mike Brown compliments Raptors coach despite him mocking Jalen Brunson during clash
articles.summary: Toronto Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic made it clear that he was not a fan of New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson flopping during their game. The Knicks...
articles.body:
Toronto Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic made it clear that he was not a fan of New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson flopping during their game.

The Knicks picked up a 111-102 win over the Kawhi Leonard-less Toronto Raptors on November 17 to improve their record to 8-6 for the season.

Brunson is overcoming his slow start to the season and put up 31 points, five rebounds and five assists in the win. However, his on-court antics seem to run Raptors coach Rajakovic the wrong way.

Mike Brown impressed by Darko Rajakovic even after he mocked Jalen Brunson's flopping during Knicks vs. Raptors

Rajakovic was caught on camera imitating Brunson for flopping after a shot, with cameras catching how openly Rajakovic mocked Brunson after that play.

"Darko does a heckuva job…those guys play hard, really good defensively, give us fits. I thought our execution, especially down stretch at a pretty high level both ends of the floor, in particular, offensively… Our pace, spacing, screening, take care of basketball down stretch.

Brunson had the last laugh, leading the Knicks to a much-needed win over the Raptors and establishing themselves as an East contender after a slow start to the season.

Brunson is averaging 27.0 points, 5.9 assists and 2.9 rebounds this season, and shooting 7.2 free throws per game. He ranks 11th in free-throw attempts this season, so his flopping hasn't helped him get to the line much.

Brunson's scoring is the key offensive weapon the Knicks are built around, evidenced by his performances in their run to the 2026 NBA Championship.

While Rajakovic did not do anything excessive in terms of complaining about Brunson's actions, he did display his feelings in a hilarious fashion.

This was Toronto's fifth straight loss of this season, falling to 5-9 on the season. Rajakovic has the support of the organisation and likely felt comfortable calling out Brunson with his gesture instead of biting his tongue.

However, complaining about calls will not change the Raptors' fortunes this season, as evidenced by the loss to the Knicks.

articles.title: Los Lakers se salvan in extremis gracias a los 83 puntos anotados entre Doncic y Quentin Grimes
articles.standfirst: Los Lakers remontan 18 puntos de desventaja para sumar su novena victoria consecutiva en un histórico partido de Quentin Grimes (47 puntos)
articles.summary: Los Lakers remontan 18 puntos de desventaja para sumar su novena victoria consecutiva en un histórico partido de Quentin Grimes (47 puntos)
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers remontaron 18 puntos de desventaja y ganaron en la prórroga a los Charlotte Hornets por 118-114 gracias a los 83 puntos que sumaron entre Luka Doncic y Quentin Grimes. Luka Doncic (36 puntos (13 de 34 en tiros de campo), 6 rebotes, 7 asistencias, 1 robo y 1 tapón) y Quentin Grimes (47 puntos con 10 de 14 en triples) no pudieron evitar la derrota de los de púrpura y oro. JJ Redick, entrenador de los Lakers, desveló tras el partido que Doncic quería hacerle llegar el balón al enrachado Quentin Grimes para cerrar el partido: "Cuando volvió al encuentro en el último cuarto Luka descartaba una y otra vez cada jugada que yo proponía... él se daba cuenta de lo que estaba ocurriendo". Quentin Grimes acabó forzando la prórroga que salvó a los Lakers, que sumó su noveno triunfo consecutivo, con un canastón a falta de dos segundos. Quentin Grimes se unió a Kobe Bryant como el único jugador en la historia de los Lakers con al menos 10 triples en un solo partido. "Es un honor usar esta camiseta y ser mencionado junto a un tipo como Kobe", confesó. Collin Sexton (10 puntos) fue el otro jugador de los angelinos que logró dobles dígitos. Brandon Miller (28 puntos), Naz Reid (23 puntos y 11 rebotes) y Coby White (19 puntos) se quedaron a un paso de conquistar el Crypto.com Arena con los Hornets.

articles.title: Quentin Grimes makes 10 3-pointers, drops career-high 47 points to lift Lakers past Hornets
articles.summary: Quentin Grimes hit a 3-pointer in the final moments of regulation to force overtime on Tuesday night at Crypto.com Arena.
articles.body:
It took a historic outing from Quentin Grimes, but the Los Angeles Lakers' winning streak is alive and well.

Grimes hit 10 3-pointers, including a clutch bucket at the end of regulation to force overtime at Crypto.com Arena, to lift the Lakers to a 118-114 win over the Charlotte Hornets for their ninth consecutive victory. Grimes finished the night with a career-high 47 points in the outing and went 10-of-14 from behind the arc.

Grimes is now one of just two players in Lakers franchise history to record 10 made 3-pointers in a single game, joining Hall of Famer Kobe Bryant, who hit 12 in a game back in 2003.

For a long time on Tuesday night, it looked as if the Hornets were going to run away with the game. They built an 18-point lead in the third quarter, and limited the Lakers to just a layup from Grimes over nearly a six-minute span in the period. The game felt over.

But the Lakers slowly chipped away at that lead to get into position to make it a game again down the stretch. That's when Grimes drilled his most important bucket. With just seconds left on the clock and the Lakers down by three, Grimes caught a perfect pass from Luka Dončić and sank his shot from the wing.

At that point, any momentum that the Hornets had was gone. The Lakers outscored them 7-3 in the extra frame to secure the four-point win.

Grimes went 16 of 24 from the field, and had six rebounds and three assists to go with his 47-point outing. Grimes joined the Lakers this past offseason on a four-year, $60 million deal in free agency after spending last season with the Philadelphia 76ers.

"At times, it felt like he was single-handedly bringing us back," Lakers coach JJ Redick said of Grimes, via the OC Register's Benjamin Royer .

Dončić had 36 points, 7 assists and 6 rebounds in the win for the Lakers. They now sit at 13-3 on the season, which is the best record in the league.

Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 28 points in the loss, which dropped them to 4-10 on the season. Naz Reid added 23 points and 11 rebounds, and Coby White finished with 19 points.

While Tuesday night's game had a thrilling finish, the Lakers won't have much time to recover. They'll host the Utah Jazz next on Wednesday night in their third back-to-back of the season.

But at least for now, the Lakers' winning streak, and place atop the league standings, is safe.
