articles.title: Luka Deferred to Quentin Grimes, 'Was Unbelievable to Watch' in Lakers' OT Win vs. Hornets
articles.summary: Luka Dončić is the Los Angeles Lakers' unquestioned offensive engine, but on Tuesday night, he was more than happy to take on a complementary role.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić is the Los Angeles Lakers' unquestioned offensive engine, but on Tuesday night, he was more than happy to take on a complementary role.

The Lakers won their ninth straight game on Tuesday, beating the Charlotte Hornets 118-114 in overtime, and they did it on the back of Quentin Grimes, who led all scorers with 47 points.

Dončić credited Grimes with helping the Lakers overcome what was a 13-point deficit entering the fourth quarter, telling reporters , "Q got us back in the game. I was trying to get him the ball, as he deserved. What an amazing game from him ... it was unbelievable to watch."

Lakers head coach JJ Redick confirmed Dončić's version of events, as he told reporters , "Luka, when he got back in the game in the fourth, he kept he kept calling off every play I was calling and just saying, 'No, I'm trying to get Q the ball!' He recognized what was happening. The hot-hand theory ... it's a real thing. It definitely was a real thing tonight."

Dončić won his second career scoring title last season, and he is well on his way to a third this season, as he leads the league with 39.0 points per game.

Because of that, it isn't often that Luka deferring to a teammate offensively makes much sense, but Grimes' shooting display could not be ignored on Tuesday.

Per ESPN's Dave McMenamin , Grimes became only the second player in Lakers history to make double-digit three-pointers in a game, joining the legendary Kobe Bryant.

Of Grimes' 10 trifectas, none was bigger than the three-ball he hit with 1.7 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter to send the game to OT.

Dončić found a wide-open Grimes on that play, and Grimes admitted after the game that he was surprised nobody was guarding him, telling reporters , "I don't know why they left me open ... I don't think I would have left me open."

Luka and Grimes combined to finish the job in overtime, as Dončić hit the go-ahead bucket, and Grimes added some insurance points with two free throws.

With Dončić dropping 36 points of his own, he and Grimes combined for a remarkable 83 points on Tuesday. No other Lakers player scored more than 10.

A lack of secondary scoring isn't usually a recipe of success, but the Lakers were able to overcome it against the Hornets thanks largely to Grimes' efficient scoring.

The Lakers, who lead the NBA with a 13-2 record, will look to continue rolling and make it 10 wins in a row on Wednesday when they host the Utah Jazz.

articles.title: Tyran Stokes Injured, Latest on Top NBA Prospect and Bill Self's Reaction After Kansas' Win
articles.summary: Kansas freshman guard and potential 2027 No. 1 overall NBA draft pick Tyran Stokes left the Jayhawks' 102-77 win over UNLV on Tuesday night with an apparent leg injury.
articles.body:
Kansas freshman guard and potential 2027 No. 1 overall NBA draft pick Tyran Stokes left the Jayhawks' 102-77 win over UNLV on Tuesday night with an apparent leg injury.

According to ESPN's Jeff Borzello , Stokes went down to the court early in the second half and appeared to point at his knee. Stokes was helped off the court and did not return, although Borzello noted that he was seen walking under his own power in the hallway.

Kansas head coach Bill Self characterized the injury as "lower leg" in nature, telling reporters that he would not know the severity until the MRI results come in.

"It's a lower leg deal," Self said. "He lost strength in his leg, and that's why he sat down. I don't know anything more than that. So, MRI will probably tell us what the issue is.

"It didn't look bad to me, but sometimes things that don't look bad can be more serious than things that actually do look bad. So, I'll reserve comment on the seriousness because we have no idea."

Stokes, 19, was rated by 247Sports as the No. 1 recruit in the nation when he landed with Kansas back in April.

Through four games for the 11th-ranked Jayhawks, Stokes has shown why he was deserving of that lofty distinction, averaging 14.8 points per contest on 50.0 percent shooting from the field and 46.2 percent shooting from deep to go along with 8.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.5 three-pointers made.

The versatile, 6'8" star was at his best in an 89-69 blowout win over then-No. 24 Kentucky last week.

Stokes scored a career-high 23 points and also recorded his first career double-double, adding 10 rebounds.

Despite playing only 13 minutes and missing most of the second half, Stokes had another double-double on Tuesday with 13 points and 10 boards.

Stokes has been a driving force behind Kansas' 4-0 start, and losing him for any period of time would represent a significant loss, especially with games against major programs such as West Virginia, Villanova, UConn and Ohio State on tap over the next month.

An extended absence could also adversely impact Stokes' push to go first overall in the 2027 NBA draft.

In his latest mock draft released on Tuesday, Bleacher Report NBA draft expert Jonathan Wasserman projected Stokes to go first overall to the New Orleans Pelicans.

That could still come to fruition even if Stokes misses time, but it would open the door for Arizona's Caleb Holt, Illinois' Quentin Coleman, BYU's Bruce Branch III and others to establish themselves as contenders for the No. 1 overall pick during his absence.

articles.title: Are the Heat suddenly a threat in the East? How Giannis Antetokounmpo is making an impact in Miami
articles.summary: The Heat are riding a five-game winning streak and operating like a top-10 unit on both ends of the floor during this run.
articles.body:
MIAMI — It's go-time for Giannis Antetokounmpo.

There's nothing fancy about the start of this possession. Giannis inbounds the ball to Davion Mitchell, who trots up the left sideline while Giannis fills the middle of the floor. Mitchell pitches it back to Giannis above the break, with Rockets center Alperen Şengün tasked with navigating whatever comes next.

Two dribbles to the left. A gather and spin to the right — through the arms of Şengün — into a lefty layup.

A little over a minute later, it's time for a Mitchell-Giannis pick-and-roll in the middle of the floor. Klay Thompson, Miami's resident flame-thrower, is stationed in the left corner, but he won't stay there.

Mitchell begins his attack, taking three dribbles on his way to Paint Touch City. While Mitchell attacks, Thompson lifts to the left wing to put Kevin Durant in a pickle. Fulfill his low-man duties — tag Giannis on the roll so he doesn't have a lob opportunity — or follow Thompson so he doesn't receive a kickout for a 3.

Durant chooses the latter, giving Giannis an acre of space to roll into.

Two more points after Mitchell promptly tosses a lob.

Following a missed pull-up 3 from Fred VanVleet, the ball finds Giannis' hands after a rebound scramble. Seven seconds later, Giannis adds a transition bucket to his third-quarter resume.

Next, it's a left elbow touch against Jabari Smith Jr. that ends in free throws — he makes both.

Two minutes later, it's a transition spin-and-finish against Smith Jr.

Then it's another transition attack, this time with Tari Eason and a late-arriving Isaiah Crawford as and-1 victims.

Finally, it's a left block touch against Eason, who fights his tail off to prevent Giannis from establishing deep positioning. His reward? Giannis converting another and-1 immediately after receiving an entry pass from Ryan Conwell.

It's a 14-point quarter for the former MVP, and that's without getting into the four assists he dished out. What made this particular outburst special is when it happened.

It was a tone-setting, game-sealing third quarter — the infamous "turd quarter" for those in the know; it should come as no surprise that the Heat are, once again, in the negative to start the year — that the Heat needed with Bam Adebayo being held out due to right hip tightness.

(He's since been listed as "probable" for Wednesday night's game against the Milwaukee Bucks — Giannis' first matchup against his former team.)

There were natural questions about what non-Giannis minutes would look like in a Bam-less context; because of Giannis' dominant quarter, the Heat got to navigate those waters in the fourth quarter, with a 20-point lead as a buffer.

It was also helpful that Giannis didn't need to turn on that level of aggression in the first half. Miami's defense was ironclad in the first half, and it got plenty of scoring production from the others — headlined by Conwell's 12 off the bench, and Thompson's 11 — allowing Giannis to simply defend, rebound, distribute and utilize his superstar gravity to unlock things for others. "He was Magic Johnson for the first 14 minutes of the game," Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra told reporters after the game .

"And when he needed to be aggressive, he found different ways to get downhill and do what he does," Spoelstra said. "He wasn't a bull in a china shop to start the game; it was setting everyone up. That's what we're talking about: exponential impact. He can have that exponential impact on our offense just by being who he is — arguably, on any given night, the best player in the league."

There's context to sprinkle in on the Rockets' side — they were on the second night of a road back-to-back, down Amen Thompson and others (Steven Adams and Marcus Smart chief among them) — but Monday's 128-110 win over the Rockets was arguably the Heat's most complete win of the season.

Here the Heat sit, riding a five-game winning streak and operating like a top-10 unit on both ends of the floor during this run.

Per Cleaning The Glass, the Heat sit eighth in overall offensive rating (117.6) while sporting the third-ranked half-court offense (101.8, 5.8 points above league average) in the league. It's an outstanding place to be considering the preseason expectations — potentially explosive, but likely a clunky unit as the personnel got used to each other.

The largest baseline question entering the year was two-pronged: how well would Giannis slot into Miami's screens-are-optional system from last season, and how much would the Heat bend on said-principles to accommodate Giannis' skill set?

Broken into three intervals — Miami's first four games, their next five games, and the current five-game winning streak — here's what their rate of screening (on and off the ball), dribble handoff (DHO) work, and the success of drives (plus the percentage of drives they're seeing help defenders) looks like with Giannis on the floor compared to last year. All numbers, per 100 possessions, courtesy of Second Spectrum:

And here is how Giannis has fared in those contexts compared to last season:

In summary: the Heat have certainly incorporated more screening and handoff work into the offense than last year, with everything aside from off-ball screening trending up as the season sample grows. Giannis specifically has been less involved in actions compared to last year, but that screening context has arguably made life easier for his teammates (more on that shortly) while the general spacing construct has led to clearer driving lanes than he's used to seeing.

We knew that Spoelstra was going to work diligently to find the right balance of everything. When to put the ball in Giannis' hands and where; when to space him, and where; who to pair him in actions with. Those questions were (and are) most important in relation to his All-Star frontcourt partner, Bam Adebayo.

With neither being shooters that strike fear into the hearts of defenses, there was a natural clunkiness they'd have to work through. During the Heat's 0-4 start, Adebayo struggled to make shots, and Giannis had pockets of indecision when trying to assert himself.

A quieter observation was how clunky their (re)spacing felt; the amount of times Giannis would perform an ill-timed (or ill-paced) cut during an Adebayo post touch was, well, let's just call it #LessThanIdeal.

(As a brief aside: Giannis (59) and Adebayo (55) rank third and fourth in total post-ups this year. A Spo team leading the NBA in post-ups? Who had that on their preseason bingo card?)

A notable setup that's emerged as of late: pick-and-rolls involving one as the screener, while the other is spaced in the dunker spot . It serves the early benefit of clearing space above the break so those ball screens can develop:

Giving Giannis or Adebayo space in the middle of the floor can feel perilous. Both are having tremendous midrange shooting seasons at the moment, but it's more important that they have room to load up for paint touches.

Because they're threatening finishers — Antetokounmpo in particular is one of the best in league history — it forces teams to help in different ways, unlocking passing reads (corner kick-outs in particular) that both are good enough to capitalize on, quickly.

Nickeil Alexander has to make a decision between providing extra relief to prevent a pass to Adebayo, or staying home to prevent a corner pass to Pelle Larsson:

With Alexander-Walker flowing toward Adebayo, Giannis promptly makes the swing to Larsson against Alexander-Walker's momentum for an open 3:

(Another aside: There's also the benefit of having a tremendous athlete near the basket for offensive rebound opportunities. Though they didn't all come from dunker spot lurking, it's worth noting that Giannis and Adebayo combined for nine offensive rebounds in that Hawks game.)

On the year, the Heat have logged 43 picks with one of Giannis or Adebayo as a screener, with the other in the dunker spot. They've generated an absurd 1.26 points per trip in that context, giving shades of a potential "end game" setup with more reps.

It's important, according to Spoelstra , that the Heat don't lean on any singular thing. Being able to seamlessly flow between different spacing alignments and different actions is where the Heat ultimately want to get to.

"I know I say it all the time, but it doesn't necessarily matter what the trigger is," Spoelstra told reporters ahead of Monday's win against the Rockets.

"Sometimes the trigger may be a pitch-ahead drive; it might be a pick-and-roll; it might be a post-up. I think we're developing more out of our menu, more diversity. If we just go to one thing all of the time, that efficiency will probably go down."

"Right now, we're tapping into quite a few different things. Hopefully, while we're doing that, we're going to guys' specific strengths. But it does take some trust, for the guys to be open to doing some things that might be a little bit different than how they've done it, and then [doing] things they really feel comfortable doing. That's part of it when you have some new players and you're trying to put it all together."

Watching Giannis lurk around the dunker spot or act as a screening or handoff hub for perimeter players aren't new concepts; he did so — and showcased he could do so at a high level — during his best years in Milwaukee. Practically doing so at the expense of some of the on-ball work — not only are the inverted pick-and-roll reps (with Giannis as the ball-handler) down, but drives in general are lower in volume — is where the adjustment comes in.

To Giannis' credit, he's been able to build real chemistry with Thompson and Mitchell in different ways. It's largely been off-ball and handoff work with Thompson; the differences in size and skill-set put defenses in a bind whenever they're in action together.

As simple as a pindown is, you have to think really hard about how you want to guard it. If you try to navigate it over the top, you run the risk of falling behind Thompson and either opening up a shot for him or, if the screener defender steps up, a passing window for a rolling Giannis.

Try to duck under a screen, and you risk Thompson sprinkling in jumper after jumper. Switch the action, and you're in double trouble. You're switching a smaller defender onto Giannis; we know he can pulverize mismatches, or at the very least, draw double teams because of the fear of pulverizing those matchups. And because Thompson doesn't stop moving without the ball, the bigger player switching onto him still has work to do.

During the win streak, the Heat have generated 1.5 PPP (!!!) on trips featuring a Giannis off-ball screen for Thompson. Their handoff partnership (1.21 PPP) has been similarly tough to deal with during this run.

With Mitchell, it's been more traditional pick-and-roll. There's been 5-out, middle-of-the floor goodness. The aforementioned dunker spot spacing (flat spacing, for the win) with plenty of room to operate with up top. With Mitchell trotting up a sideline, the two can flow into empty-side actions to further place defenses in what-do-we-do scenarios.

Mitchell has continued to grow as a ball-screen operator, weaponizing his speed (and penchant for paint touches) to generate looks for himself or others. Because he can turn on the jets at any time, he's done a better job of working at slower speeds to begin these actions. It allows his screener (Giannis in this case) to make cleaner reads; they can establish themselves to actually make contact, or more realistically sell the setup to make screen-slipping more effective weapons.

The driving cadence, the shifting of gears, and the growing timing and placement of Mitchell's passes (the quick-hitting pocket passes are simple but incredibly effective) have made him one of the league's most efficient pick-and-roll creators, even within Miami's low-volume context.

To that point, I present you two data points:

Among 42 players that have received at least 200 on-ball picks this year, Mitchell's 1.12 PPP mark ranks seventh in the league.

The Heat are generating an absurd 1.46 PPP on trips featuring a Mitchell-Giannis ball screen, tops among 52 duos to have logged at least 75 reps together.

The "exponential impact" that Spoelstra spoke to hasn't quite played out statistically, at least not yet. Giannis has made his team's offense better in every season of his career, but this year's differential (+0.4, per Cleaning The Glass) would easily be the lowest of his career.

That comes with the very obvious "lineup construction matters!" context; the thing about on-off numbers is that the "off" portion can say just as much about the backups (and the lineups they're facing) as they do about the player in question (Giannis).

But it's clear that the seeds that were planted earlier in the season are starting to bear fruit right now. The Rockets game on Monday was a loud example of Giannis being able to amplify things without needing to dictate his own terms (first half), but still being capable of doing so when the game calls for it (third quarter).

That's a formula that can only work when others pull their weight, but it's an easier one to replicate when players are empowered to do so the way they are in this offense. Mitchell is playing well; Thompson is playing free. Adebayo is finding his way and playing decisively. Youngsters like Ryan Conwell and Myron Gardner are playing freely. It's the kind of confidence-building that obviously feels loud during a winning streak, but ultimately should bode well as we get deeper into the season. Having proof-of-concept to lean on makes it easier for players to buy-in, and makes it easier to re-center things when adversity hits.

It's probably unfair to expect the Heat to maintain a 127.4 offensive rating like we've seen during the winning streak, but it should alarm the league that the Heat has this kind of juice in them.

articles.title: New Anthony Davis Trade Rumors Update Value on Wizards Star amid Contract Buzz
articles.summary: With Anthony Davis off to a strong start despite the Washington Wizards' early-season struggles, his name is popping back up as a potential trade candidate.
articles.body:
With Anthony Davis off to a strong start despite the Washington Wizards' early-season struggles, his name is popping back up as a potential trade candidate.

On the latest episode of The Hoop Collective podcast (starts at 11:16 mark), ESPN's Brian Windhorst noted there is a "demand" for Davis around the league except teams don't want to give him the type of contract he would be seeking.

"I think people have demand for Anthony Davis," Windhorst said. "They just don't want to give him a max extension, and I don't think he's looking for a max extension, but I do think he's looking for a lot of money."

Davis was a popular trade candidate over the summer, but the Wizards also made a series of in-season moves last year to acquire him and Trae Young with the hope of kickstarting a contention window.

The duo didn't play together last season because Davis was out with a hand injury, so this season is the first chance for Washington officials to evaluate how this group looks.

Two things have happened since the Davis trade that could alter any plans they initially had when they made the deal with the Dallas Mavericks in February. The first is he didn't sign an extension in part because both parties wanted to see how things played out at the start of the 2026-27 season.

The other wrinkle is the Wizards won the draft lottery and used the No. 1 pick to select AJ Dybantsa. His addition made him the most important player for the franchise going forward.

There are contract issues for Davis could impact how much value the Wizards might be able to bring back if they were to make him available. He holds a $62.8 million player option for 2027-28.

Davis has been eligible to sign an extension for up to four years and $275 million since Aug. 6. He is healthy right now and playing well for the Wizards so far. He is averaging 24.5 points, 9.8 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game in 13 starts, but Washington sits at 4-11 amid a current eight-game losing streak.

The Wizards haven't made the playoffs since the 2020-21 season. Their last season with a winning record was in 2017-18 when they finished 43-39.

articles.title: Lakers' biggest win of the year? The risky offseason move to get Walker Kessler
articles.summary: With Kessler manning the middle, the Lakers have very loudly reshaped their defensive approach.
articles.body:
When the Lakers sent two unprotected firsts and two additional swaps to the Jazz for Walker Kessler this offseason, the overwhelming consensus was that Los Angeles had hemorrhaged a significant chunk of its future flexibility for a questionable fit at best.

But when these two teams tip off against each other on Wednesday night — at least one of those worries will have already been assuaged. Kessler is an outstanding fit for the Lakers, who have won nine straight and own the best record in the NBA following a thrilling overtime win against the Hornets on Tuesday. (The Jazz, meanwhile, have the league's third-worst record.)

"Unbelievable, honestly," Luka Dončić said last month of his new teammate Kessler, who is averaging 14.5 points, 10.9 rebounds and 2.2 blocks per game. "We know what we're getting; I'm not surprised by how he's playing. He knows how to play this game, he played for a long time. I'm not surprised, but the fact that he's doing it, just proving a lot of people wrong, is just unbelievable."

After the departure of LeBron James and the re-emergence of Dončić as a centripetal force, the Lakers needed a stabilizer. Not necessarily a running mate — Austin Reaves had already proven to be a high-octane complementary piece — but a dependable back-line enforcer. The Deandre Ayton/Jaxson Hayes tandem flamed out as quickly as it started in L.A., and the days of Anthony Davis were long gone. Dončić reportedly pushed hard for Kessler, who played only five games last season in Utah after shoulder surgery.

The results speak for themselves. With Kessler on the floor, the Lakers are allowing just 111.0 points per 100 possessions, which would rank j ust outside the top-five in defensive efficiency. With Kessler manning the middle, the Lakers have very loudly reshaped their defensive approach. They're fifth in "compact" shell possessions, per Synergy tracking data, which refers to the surface area connecting all five defenders on the floor. Last season, the Lakers ranked 22nd in that category.

Constricting the restricted area certainly comes with trade-offs, too. Contenders like Oklahoma City and San Antonio were notorious for similar styles in recent years, being comfortable with giving up 3s in the corners and essentially anywhere else on the perimeter. And to that point, the Lakers are dead last in opponent corner attempts and 28th in overall opponent perimeter attempts. (The non-Kesslers also do a decent job of contesting despite the amount of ground they have to cover at times, with Kessler's lateral movement helping a ton in this regard.)

What the Lakers have done is dare teams to shoot and laugh at the ones that even think about attacking the rim. Only four players have fared better than Kessler with shots within six feet: Donovan Clingan, Jalen Smith, Chet Holmgren and Victor Wembanyama. Opponents shoot nearly 13% worse when Kessler is on the floor and spend far less time venturing into his restricted area office. (He's in the 99th percentile in rim points saved .)

And don't make the mistake of thinking Kessler's presence is limited to the paint alone. He is once again posting ridiculous steal and block rates at his position, is capable of stepping outside to contest and bother shots and continues to be active in passing lanes. Pairing a talent like that with Matisse Thybulle, who's basically been the best defensive playmaker in basketball for a few seasons now , gives the Lakers the necessary juice to be the league's best in opponent turnover rate.

"You're talking about one of the best rim protectors in the NBA," JJ Redick said last week. "And that doesn't always show up in blocked shots or steals. He's doing a fantastic job for us."

At the other end, Kessler's value comes with the understanding that the Lakers aren't asking him to step outside of his comfort zone. Sure, Dončić as arguably the best player in the world helps a ton, using his gravity and elite on-ball talent to draw defenders out and create space. But Kessler knows where to find impact. He's quick enough to zoom around the perimeter, screen for his guards and duck under slower bigs to find pockets of space around the rim. And the Lakers know how to use his mobility (although it comes at the expense of their defensive rebounding at times). Kessler has accumulated nearly triple the number of possessions as a cutter or in transition (48) as he has as a roll man (17). He understands the assignment; he's in the 92nd percentile in points per shot attempt, albeit at a low usage rate.

"He's just healthy," one scout told Yahoo Sports. "He's a high-IQ big, active and young. Youth and health are the biggest things working well for Walker and that's helping their defense as a whole. [On offense] he's intelligent. He knows how to play his role; screen, roll, catch lobs and putbacks, and finish. He's not doing anything outside of his skill set."

Two areas you'd like to see improvement in are his touch/strength and finishing rate. Kessler is in the 98th percentile in rim attempts, but just 75th in conversion , as well as 34th percentile in ball security. Dončić's gravity dictates a plethora of paint touches, which Kessler leads the league in, but more aggression should help in that department.

Detractors will point to the Lakers' strength of schedule (five of their wins in the current nine-game run have been against teams with losing records), but bah humbug. They are taking care of business, and have helped Kessler settle in quickly. And, from Utah's vantage point, the Lakers' big acquisition this summer is enjoying the much greener SoCal grass.

articles.title: El apellido Stojakovic vuelve a sonar: 46 puntos que hacen historia para profanar el templo de Duke
articles.standfirst: Andrej, hijo de Peja Stojakovic, bate el récord anotador de un rival en el mítico pabellón de los Blue Devils
articles.summary: Andrej, hijo de Peja Stojakovic, bate el récord anotador de un rival en el mítico pabellón de los Blue Devils
articles.body: El apellido Stojakovic ha vuelto a sonar con fuerza en Estados Unidos. Andrej, hijo del Peja, uno de los mejores tiradores de siempre en la NBA, firmó una actuación histórica al anotar 46 puntos frente a la legendaria Universidad de Duke. El escolta de 22 años y 2,01 metros que milita en la Universidad de Illinois consiguió la mayor anotación jamás registrada por un jugador rival en el Cameron Indoor Stadium, hogar de los Blue Devils, batiendo un registro que databa de febrero de 1957, cuando Grady Wallace metió 43 puntos con South Carolina. Andrej se quedó a sólo un punto del récord de cualquier rival ante Duke. Esa marca la posee Ernie Beck, que metió 47 con Pennsylvania en 1952. Y a dos puntos de igualar a Dick Groat, de Duke, también en 1952, como el jugador con más puntos en los casi 87 años de historia del Cameron. Hablamos de marcas de hace 70 años. "Mis compañeros creyeron en mí desde el principio. Creo que merecen reconocimiento por haberme apoyado. Esa es la belleza de este equipo. Aquí no hay egos. Y cualquiera podría tener su noche, dijo Stojakovic, que ya llevaba 20 puntos al descanso y acabó con 14/21 en tiros de campo (sólo 2/3 en triples) y 16/20 desde la personal. Con su hito ayudó a su equipo a ganar por un contundente 78-99. Fue la derrota en casa más abultada para Duke desde el 5 de marzo de 1983, cuando North Carolina venció por una diferencia de 24 puntos y un tal Michael Jordan se fue hasta los 32. Con este derrota, los Blue Devils también vieron acabar una racha de 35 victorias consecutivas como locales. "No he participado en un partido así desde que estoy aquí, ni como jugador ni como entrenador. Hay que reconocerle el mérito a Stojakovic: el partido que hizo fue histórico", dijo Jon Scheyer, entrenador de Duke, con pasado como jugador en el Gran Canaria. "Stojakovic es un gran jugador. Estuvo imparable y no pude detenerle", dijo Dame Sarr, ex del Barça, uno de los que tuvo que defenderle. Andrej es hijo de Peja Stojakovic, que jugó 804 partidos en la NBA enrolado en los Kings, donde se le retiró la camiseta, Pacers, Pelicans, Raptors y Mavericks, con los que ganó el anillo en 2011 antes de retirarse. En su carrera promedió 17,0 puntos con un sensacional 40,1% en triples y un 89,5% en tiros libres, uno de los mejores porcentajes de la historia. Fue tres veces All Star y ganó el concurso de triples en dos ocasiones. El joven Andrej nació en Salónica, de padre serbio y madre griega, con lo que posee la doble nacionalidad, aunque parece que se decantará por la última en su carrera profesional. Creció en California y al acabar el instituto recibió ofertas de algunas de las mejores Universidades de Estado Unidos: UCLA, Florida, Indiana, Kentucky, Texas, Stanford... Se decantó por esta última, aunque sólo permaneció un año antes de trasladarse a California. Allí promedió 17,9 puntos la temporada pasada. Y en verano, otra mudanza, a Illinois. En las previsiones del draft de la NBA no aparece en los puestos de arriba. De hecho, no estaría ni entre los 50 mejores proyectos de la próxima edición. Quizás suba con actuaciones así.

articles.title: Hannah Hidalgo Drops Confident Quote After Tempo Win 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery
articles.summary: Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo says she feels she will go ahead of other stars including USC's JuJu Watkins in the upcoming WNBA draft after the Toronto Tempo won the draft lottery earlier this week.
articles.body:
Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo says she feels she will go ahead of other stars including USC's JuJu Watkins in the upcoming WNBA draft after the Toronto Tempo won the draft lottery earlier this week.

"My goal is to go the highest pick," Hidalgo told CBS Sports' Isabel Gonzalez about her approach to the season. "To go No. 1 and to whatever team, of course it's Toronto.

"My goal is to go No. 1 and I'm going to do everything this season to show that I'm the No. 1 pick."

Hidalgo is leading women's college basketball with 28.3 points per game through four contests of her senior season with the Fighting Irish.

She is also tied for fourth in the nation with 4.8 steals per game while averaging 7.5 assists and 5.5 rebounds during Notre Dame's 4-0 run through non-conference play.

Even if Hidalgo keeps up that production down the stretch of the season, her officially listed height of 5'7" could raise some concerns regarding her ability to replicate that success in the WNBA.

Bleacher Report's latest WNBA mock draft features the Tempo selecting Watkins with the No. 1 pick before the Houston Comets select Texas' Madison Booker and the Washington Mystics pick LSU's Mikaylah Williams.

B/R then projects Hidalgo will go to the Seattle Storm with the No. 4 pick of the upcoming draft after dropping out of the top three due in part to what Bleacher Report's Jack Bonin described as concerns regarding her ability to overcome her size at the next level.

Hidalgo has posted a career 33.6 shooting percentage from deep so far in her college career, and Bonin noted her offensive upside could be "limited" outside of the point guard position.

"Hidalgo should be a great defender in the league, but there are questions as to how much her size limits her against WNBA athletes," Bonin wrote. "If Hidalgo is simply a good defender instead of an All-Defensive one, how high is her ceiling?"

There are fewer size concerns regarding Watkins, who is listed at 6'2" and has earned buzz as a potential top pick since before she debuted at USC in 2023.

After sitting out the entirety of the 2025-26 season amid recovery from an ACL injury, Watkins has averaged 24.5 points and 6.8 rebounds per game through her first four contests back in the Trojans lineup.

Hidalgo may face an uphill battle to prove she can provide more of an impact at the next level than Watkins or Booker (6'1") and Williams (6'0") as Notre Dame gears up to begin ACC play this December.

articles.title: Lakers Must Trade for Key Center amid Latest NBA Rumors Despite Being No. 1 in West Standings
articles.summary: Life atop the NBA is, objectively speaking, fun as heck.
articles.body:
Life atop the NBA is, objectively speaking, fun as heck.

Just ask the Los Angeles Lakers, who possess the league's best winning percentage (.867) and arguably roster the MVP frontrunner in Luka Dončić, who has cleared 30 points in 11 consecutive contests.

But even great teams have issues to clean up, and L.A. is no exception there. The backup center role has been a sore spot for a while now, and it's a problem that likely needs correcting on the trade market.

Luckily, the Lakers seemingly know where to look. They were reportedly among the teams to give "attention" to New Orleans Pelicans reserve Karlo Matković this offseason, per Heavy.com's Sean Deveney , and Matković's solid start to the season should only pique the Purple and Gold's interest in him.

The third-year combo big pairs legitimate three-point touch (38.6 percent this season, 38 even for his career) with above-the-rim athleticism.

It isn't hard to envision Matković thriving as a screen-setter for L.A.'s star guards, either popping out to the perimeter or rolling hard to the rim. If nothing else, he would give this group a change-of-pace option from its more traditional starting center Walker Kessler.

It's even easier to picture Matković making much more of an impact than the Lakers' current backup bigs. Save for the streaky Sandro Mamukelashvili, who splits his time between the 4 and 5 spots, the pickings have been slim. Kevon Looney lost his rotation role before October ended, and two-way rookie Carson Cooper just debuted after inking his deal earlier this month.

Now, clearly the Lakers have been winning in spite of this weakness. Their prominent position atop the Western Conference standings clearly (and convincingly) attests to that.

Has the schedule helped out with that success? Probably , but there are only so many ways to nitpick winning 13 games in 15 tries.

L.A. almost certainly has enough to keep this regular-season run going. Still, this group holds greater ambitions than that.

"Wins right now are great, but wins in the postseason are better," Lakers swingman Mattise Thybulle told reporters .

In other words, the Lakers can't allow these early triumphs to distract them from the larger task at hand. This isn't their measuring stick. They have to hold themselves to a higher standard, because, if everything goes according to plan, there will be much greater challenges ahead.

That's why the front office can't let roster imperfections linger. Especially one as obvious as this.

Matković might not be a needle-mover, but he would help shore up perhaps the team's most glaring problem so far. That matters, particularly when the acquisition cost can't be overwhelming. ( As intriguing as he looks on paper, he's still a sub-20 minute reserve averaging 7.4 points and 3.9 rebounds .)

The Lakers could aim higher than this , of course, but doing so would cut deeper into what's already a depleted asset collection. If cost effectiveness plays a big part in the backup big man pursuit, then Matković might best straddle the intersection between value and impact.

articles.title: Heat Trading for Giannis Compared to Carmelo Joining Knicks as NBA Execs Doubt Roster for Title Run
articles.summary: The Miami Heat made an all-in move by acquiring two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo over the offseason, but not everyone is convinced that it will pay off.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat made an all-in move by acquiring two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo over the offseason, but not everyone is convinced that it will pay off.

ESPN's Tim MacMahon spoke to multiple executives who expressed doubts over whether the Heat will be able to contend for a championship in their first year with Antetokounmpo leading the way.

"It's kind of like when the Knicks traded for Carmelo," an Eastern Conference executive said, referring to an era when New York won a total of one playoff series in Carmelo Anthony's 6½-year tenure with the franchise. "You trade all your average players and gut your depth and then try to replace it with minimums and bargain contracts."

The Heat gave up Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis, the rights to 2026 No. 13 pick Nate Ament and four more future draft picks to acquire Antetokounmpo and veteran forward Bobby Portis from the Milwaukee Bucks. After starting the season with a 0-4 record, Miami has improved to 8-6 and is riding a five-game win streak into Wednesday's game against Milwaukee, which marks Antetokounmpo's first meeting against his old squad.

MacMahon explained that the "belief of several scouts and executives polled by ESPN is that the Heat lack the supporting cast around Antetokounmpo and [Bam] Adebayo to make a deep playoff run." Even with strong starts by veteran shooting guard Klay Thompson and rising point guard Davion Mitchell, many feel that Miami will have to "upgrade its starting backcourt before being a legitimate threat to come out of the East."

"Are they going to be able to get into the top four in the East and win a playoff series?" an executive on another Eastern Conference team said. "I think that's very realistic. But that's usually not the bar for a team that makes an all-in trade."

Despite the doubters from around the league, the confidence is reportedly high in South Beach.

"We're very confident in our team," a Heat source told MacMahon. "We believe we have a chance in the East along with everybody else [considered a contender]. We're not waiting. We want to win now."

Antetokounmpo has played just 14 games in a Miami uniform, so the team feels that it's too early to determine what pieces are needed around him.

"[Pat Riley's] line has always been that it takes 20 games to figure out what you need," the Heat source added. "Then, what are your opportunities?"

While it may not be a quick turnaround, Miami is expected to eventually find its way to title contention, even if the team has to wait another year.

"I don't think they were expecting this to be overnight, that they'd immediately be a contender," a West executive said. "They're going to have to figure some things out. I'm sure they will."

articles.title: Why the over 148.5 is the play for UConn vs. Arizona in Wednesday's ranked matchup
articles.summary: UConn, ranked 3rd at 4-0, faces its first true road test against Arizona as the over 148.5 is the play in this top college basketball matchup.
articles.body: It was a true disaster for me with college hoops yesterday. As soon as I bet it, I felt like the Duke pick was a bad call, and it was. Michigan State was just as bad. We have some great games on Wednesday as well. I’m really excited for some of today’s games because we do see some ranked matchups again. Ranked games aren’t always the best, but we have some fun ones to watch, and UConn vs. Arizona is definitely the top matchup of the night. UConn comes into the game as a newly minted third team in the nation with a 4-0 record for the season. The Huskies have had a couple of tough battles to start the year, and a couple of cupcake matchups. They started the year with a 40-point win over Gardner-Webb. Their next game was against Michigan, the team that beat them in the National Championship game last year, and they got a little bit of revenge, winning by eight. The Huskies dominated Wagner by 42, and then Friday they took down Ohio State, winning by 14. We know there are certain times teams struggle. One of them is when they play on the road, and UConn has to do that for the first time. Sure, the game against Michigan was in TD Garden in Boston, but that was closer to a home game than a true road test. Most of these guys have played in really tough games and hard road battles, but traveling across the country to play a tough team is never easy. I’m interested to see how Braylon Mullins performs in this one. He is shooting 42.9% overall, 83.3% from the charity stripe, and 37.1% from the three-point line. UCONN, KANSAS AND TEXAS OFFER THE BEST COLLEGE BASKETBALL NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP ODDS VALUE Arizona is one of the better teams in the country, but I wouldn’t necessarily classify the Wildcats as a title contender. articles.title: Heat rumors: Why many NBA insiders aren’t buying Miami’s hot streak translating into contender status
articles.summary: After a slow start, the Miami Heat have been rolling over the past few games. Following a 20-point loss to the Warriors, they are on a five-game win streak,...
articles.body:
After a slow start, the Miami Heat have been rolling over the past few games. Following a 20-point loss to the Warriors, they are on a five-game win streak, and it appears that things are finally clicking. But many outside observers of the Heat believe that, while they are surging during their win streak and ascending to the fourth seed in the Eastern Conference standings, they still aren't contenders.

ESPN's Tim MacMahon reported that several scouts and executives he polled believe Miami's supporting cast isn't strong enough around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo for a deep playoff run, and that the Heat will need to upgrade their starting backcourt despite good starts from Davion Mitchell and Klay Thompson.

One executive from another Eastern Conference team told ESPN that making the playoffs would be realistic, but that it's not the standard for a team that makes an all-in trade.

"Are they going to be able to get into the top four in the East and win a playoff series?" an executive on another Eastern Conference team said. "I think that's very realistic. But that's usually not the bar for a team that makes an all-in trade."

MacMahon also noted that, even though Miami has climbed to the fourth seed, DraftKings has the Heat with only the seventh-best odds to win the East. But ESPN's Richard Jefferson, on the latest edition of the Road Trippin' podcast, was bullish on the Heat's chances as a contender based on Klay Thompson's recent play.

"Right now, if they were entering into a playoff series, and Klay's shooting like that, they look like they can contend with anybody."

articles.title: Wizards Firing HC Keefe Eyed by NBA Execs amid Losing Record with Anthony Davis, Dybantsa, Young
articles.summary: ESPN's Brian Windhorst says some people around the NBA are speculating the Washington Wizards could potentially extend their window with Anthony Davis by firing head coach Brian Keefe.
articles.body:
ESPN's Brian Windhorst says some people around the NBA are speculating the Washington Wizards could potentially extend their window with Anthony Davis by firing head coach Brian Keefe.

Davis is currently playing on the final guaranteed year of his contract, which features a player option for 2027-28, while leading the Wizards in scoring during the team's 4-11 start to the season.

"The other thing people are watching is if the Wizards contemplate a coaching change... and if there's a coaching change, whether or not that would buy them a reset," Windhorst said in Wednesday's episode of Brian Windhorst and the Hoop Collective (20:45 mark of the video below). "Because they kind of said let's look 20 to 30 games, and the AD side heard that, they can't force him into a contract, or force him into a trade. So AD has shown up and played.

"The question is, do the Wizards stick to that, and how does Anthony Davis react? And if there is indeed a coaching change there, does that extend that window?"

Davis has been eligible to sign an extension since August. He told reporters in September he would make a decision on his $62.8 million player option after the season, per The Athletic's David Aldridge .

Aldridge and The Athletic's Josh Robbins reported in October teams around the NBA know Davis and his representatives are seeking something "at, or very near" his maximum of $275 million over four years on his next deal.

Windhorst said on Wednesday's episode he didn't think Davis is "looking for a max extension, but I do think he's looking for a lot of money."

Keefe took over for Wes Unseld in Washington midway through the 2023-24 campaign. The Wizards have posted a combined 35-129 record while rebuilding throughout his first full two seasons as head coach.

The Wizards were likely looking to take a step forward in Keefe's third full season after adding two veterans in Davis and Trae Young at least year's deadline and drafting AJ Dybantsa at the top of the 2026 draft, but the team has so far looked uncompetitive against top teams while failing to get consistent production from any player outside Davis.

Unseld was fired in January 2024 after a 7-36 start to the season. General manager Will Dawkins could consider making a switch earlier this campaign if the franchise decides retaining Davis will help this young core take the next step in the franchise's rebuild.

articles.title: New NBA Trade Rumors on Andrew Wiggins, Portis, Jovic's Value as Heat Eye Title with Giannis, Bam
articles.summary: The Miami Heat might be light on trade assets if they try to retool the roster around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat might be light on trade assets if they try to retool the roster around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo.

"If you give up so much in a trade, do you still have the flexibility to put the right pieces around Giannis?" one Eastern Conference executive said to ESPN's Tim MacMahon . "The answer is not unequivocally no. They still have some stuff they can do, but they don't have a lot they can do."

MacMahon pointed to the fact the values of Andrew Wiggins and Nikola Jović have declined.

Wiggins' two-year extension "was initially widely considered to be a potentially valuable trade chip for the Heat" as his salary will fall to $16.5 million for the 2027-28 season. Instead, the 2021-22 All-Star is averaging just 9.4 points and got shifted to the bench earlier this month.

It's a similar story with Jović, who "has negative trade value," per MacMahon. He has been in and out of the lineup, and his 12.1 minutes per game are on pace to be a career low.

MacMahon posited Portis could at least be salary filler since he has a $15.6 million player option for next season. He's shooting just 31.6 percent from beyond the arc, though, so Miami will hope he begins to rediscover his long-range ability.

Given how much they gave up to land Antetokounmpo, there was a general consensus they'd probably need another full offseason to assemble the right kind of supporting cast.

Those plans may hinge on flipping Wiggins, Portis and/or Jović for upgrades or players who better fit Antetokounmpo and Adebayo. Right now, none of the three would likely yield a worthwhile return.

articles.title: Paul George Addresses NBA Retirement Timeline & His Celtics Role with Tatum After Jaylen Brown Trade
articles.summary: As Paul George is enjoying a resurgent season with the Boston Celtics, he is aware that his career is getting closer to the end and appreciates his current role operating with Jayson Tatum.
articles.body:
As Paul George is enjoying a resurgent season with the Boston Celtics, he is aware that his career is getting closer to the end and appreciates his current role operating with Jayson Tatum.

Speaking to The Athletic's Jay King , George emphasized he knew his job when the Celtics acquired him in the offseason was to do anything he could to support Tatum while also addressing his potential NBA mortality:

"I'm just not one of those guys that have to have an ego. My ego comes from what I do on the court when the ball gets thrown up and how I impact the game and how I affect the game in all aspects. My ego doesn't have to come from me stroking it or me thinking I'm bigger than someone or better than someone.

"But with that is, I know where I'm at in my career. I'm at the end of my career. Tatum, JT has (many) more years ahead of him, and he's someone that I admired from afar. And to see where he's taken his game, how much better he's gotten and him having all the tools and weapons to be the best player in the league, how can I help that? How can I support that and get him there? "

After playing a total of 78 games in two seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers, George was thought to have negative value because his contract is paying him $54.1 million in 2026-27 and has a $56.6 million in 2027-28.

The Sixers used his money for salary-matching to acquire Jaylen Brown from in a trade that also sent two first-round picks and two second-round picks to Boston in the offseason.

It's still early in the season, but the Celtics have to be thrilled with how their trade has played out so far. George is averaging 20.8 points on a career-high 44.3 percent three-point shooting in 12 starts.

George's future with the Celtics is going to be an interesting storyline if he keeps playing at this level, but it will be hard for them to lose him based on the current results.

At 36 years old, George is among the oldest active NBA players. He's also one of 14 active players with at least 17 seasons of experience.

The only regular starters among those players with at least 17 seasons are George, LeBron James, Kevin Durant, Stephen Curry and James Harden.

Even with retirement coming sooner than later, George is in a great spot to potentially win his first NBA championship this season. The Celtics' 11-3 record ranks second in the Eastern Conference and their plus-12.1 net rating leads the league.

articles.title: Al Real Madrid se le moja la pólvora en Estambul
articles.standfirst: Los blancos caen en un partido áspero que empezó 16-2 y en el que, lastrados por las pérdidas y los rebotes de ataque, anotaron 19 puntos menos de los que promediaban
articles.summary: Los blancos caen en un partido áspero que empezó 16-2 y en el que, lastrados por las pérdidas y los rebotes de ataque, anotaron 19 puntos menos de los que promediaban
articles.body: En un partido áspero y jugado a contracorriente desde el 16-2 inicial, al Real Madrid se le mojó la pólvora en Estambul quedándose muy por debajo de los registros ofensivos que suele manejar. Perdió en su visita al Besiktas por 83-79. Primera derrota a domicilio después de tres victorias seguidas. Los blancos anotaron 19 puntos menos de los que promediaban (98,5), a dos de su peor marca de la temporada y a un solo triple de igualar su registro más bajo (7). Cometieron 15 pérdidas, más que asistencias repartieron, 12, su mínimo del curso. Se podrían escudar en un casero y mal arbitraje, pero ellos estuvieron aún peor. No bastaron los esfuerzos hasta el último instante. Tampoco la buena actuación de Nick Smith Jr., que hizo 16 puntos y capitaneó el intento de remontada al inicio del último cuarto con 10 casi seguidos. Ni la verticalidad de Maledon, siempre un recurso con sus tiros libres. Hizo 14 de sus 22 puntos desde la personal. El Madrid se topó primero con un gran Wilbekin (15), después con un Lonney Walker IV siempre en su agenda de fichajes (15) y, finalmente, con la explosión anotadora de Jeffries. Venía promediando 2,5 puntos y -0,5 de valoración y sumó 20 con cuatro triples y 24, respectivamente. Se vio pronto que iba a ser una tarde incómoda para el Madrid, que arriesgaba en tiros y pases. Consecuencia, fallos y pérdidas. Smith Jr. abrió el marcador, pero luego vinieron siete tiros sin premio y cinco balones extraviados. Más de medio cuarto sin anotar que aprovechó un Besiktas con mucha más energía que su rival y lleno de entusiasmo en su primer duelo ante los blancos. Gabriel y Wilbekin, al que aún le queda cuerda, se aliaron para un 16-0 con Omoruyi como generador de juego. Con 14 abajo, tocaba remar. La penetraciones de Maledon y los primeros triples reengancharon a los madridistas: 18-15 tras un parcial de 2-13. Controlaron las pérdidas (siete en el primer cuarto y 15 al final), pero no los rebotes bajo su aro (16) y el Besiktas sacó tajada. Más de una vez fue en forma de triple. Siete metió en el segundo cuarto. Jeffries clavó tres, uno de ellos en carrera, desequilibrado y a tablero. Minutos antes, Tavares había fallado un mate solo. Contrastes. Los descansos del pívot se notaron en exceso. Se escapaban rebotes y los turcos se plantaban bajo el aro. Así que se volvieron a despegar (42-39). Maledon cerró al descanso con 45-37. Se esperó durante todo el choque uno de esos arreones del Madrid que se llevan por delante al rival en un par de minutos. Nunca llegó. Las rentas se estabilizaron en torno a los 10 puntos mientras Feliz y Luwawu-Cabarrot entraban en problemas de faltas. Ni unos buenos minutos de Jones cerraron la brecha (64-54). Smith tiró del Madrid en el arranque del último acto y le acercó a cuatro (71-67). Lástima que mezclara su acierto con algún despiste atrás que Walker no perdonó. Un tapón a Pradilla, un triple fallado por él mismo, una pérdida de Maledon... A los blancos se les iba escapando el partido cuando un triple de Jeffries y un tiro libre de Morgan tras rebote ofensivo lo dejaron pendiente de un hilo: 77-71 a 42 segundos del final. Pero aún quedaba. Feliz anotó tres veces desde la personal tras falta de Wilbekin. La siguiente defensa de los madridistas fue terrible. No sólo no hicieron falta sino que dejaron a Gabriel bajo el aro. Okeke llegó tarde y, entonces sí, justo cuando no debía, cometió personal. El 2+1 sentenciaba. Un postrero triple de Feliz ajustó a tres segundos del final (82-79) y Morgan cerró un partido incomodísimo para un Madrid muy por debajo de su nivel. Y este viernes, otra guerra incluso más cruenta: visita al campeón Olympiacos. 83 - Besiktas (18+27+19+19): Dotson (4), Wilbekin (15), Jeffries (20), Omoruyi (-), Gabriel (11) -cinco inicial- DeJulius (5), Morgan (5), Birsen (4), Walker IV (15), Zizic (4), Brown (-). 79 - Real Madrid (15+22+17+25): Feliz (13), Smith Jr. (16), Procida (-), Pradilla (2), Tavares (5) -cinco inicial-, Jones (5), Maledon (22), Luwawu-Cabarrot (8), Abalde (7), Okeke (1), Sarr (-). Árbitros: Borys Ryzhyk (Ucrania), Marcin Kowalski (Polonia) y Franko Gracin (Croacia). Eliminaron por cinco faltas a Bircen (m.32) y Gabriel (m.39). articles.title: Judge rips LSU attorneys amid SEC eligibility lawsuit: 'You put the pig out there'
articles.summary: A federal judge slammed attorneys representing LSU in court on Wednesday, one day after the Tigers added RJ Luis to their basketball roster.
articles.body:
A federal judge laid into lawyers representing LSU on Wednesday after the university claimed the SEC had "hallucinated" citations in a court filing.

Judge Annemarie Carney Axon demanded a retraction from the school and a "heartfelt" public statement expressing regret for using language that bashed the character of opposing attorneys, according to ESPN's Alex Scarborough . The hearing on Wednesday had to do with a previous filing regarding LSU's language, which had accused the SEC of supplying or hallucinating case citations, amid the larger legal battle between the university and the conference.

The SEC called the statement "scandalous and professionally insulting." Axon repeatedly questioned LSU attorney Bruce Rogers, who later admitted "they're not made-up cases." Rogers claimed the cases were only hallucinated because they didn't support the SEC's argument, and that they weren't calling out the lawyers directly.

Axon, however, said that was the "opposite" of what was written in his brief.

"You wouldn't want somebody to wrongly accuse you of hallucinating a case, knowing full well what the implication of that accusation is," Axon said, via ESPN.

Rogers then tried to argue that there was a broader definition to "hallucinated."

"We're not dressing this up, OK?" Axon replied. "You put the pig out there. There's no time for you to put lipstick on it."

Axon eventually told Rogers he could file a motion to remove the term "hallucinated" from the previous filing, but that it should include that it exhibited "poor professional judgement." Rogers, LSU and the attorney general's office must also issue "heartfelt" and "robust" public statements.

"I have to tell you, I'm so disappointed," Axon said. "If this happens one more time, you're going to be sanctioned to the fullest extent I can."

Despite the judge's orders, Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murril said she would not be apologizing.

"I cannot and will not apologize for my lawyers doing their job, and it is improper for an Alabama federal judge to compel speech from the state of Louisiana," she said . "The SEC made an egregious citation error. Their inability to explain that error is their problem, not Louisiana's."

LSU and the SEC have been in a legal battle for months now over the ability to play professional athletes.

Three players who had been rostered in NFL training camps earlier in the summer were legally cleared to join the Tigers' roster, which led to the SEC ruling that it could punish the Tigers for doing so — including via game boycotts or even expulsion from the league. The Tigers didn't end up including the three players in question on the football roster. The SEC filed a lawsuit against LSU in September over its attempts to play the three players.

But on Tuesday, LSU basketball added former Big East Player of the Year RJ Luis Jr. to its roster. Luis had played three preseason games for the Boston Celtics in 2025 after going undrafted out of St. John's, though he never played in a regular-season NBA game.

Luis was granted multiple temporary injunctions, including one on Friday that stated the SEC and NCAA could not legally penalize LSU for adding Luis to its roster. The SEC informed LSU on Monday that it wouldn't seek to punish the school.

But after LSU added Luis on Tuesday, the SEC called the decision "deeply concerning and disappointing."

"LSU's decision today to rely on its own interpretation of the court's order to justify its actions is inconsistent with the expectations and responsibilities of membership in the Southeastern Conference," the statement said. "This is a deeply concerning and disappointing development. The conference will continue to uphold and defend the standards and policies established by its member universities."

LSU football coach Lane Kiffin was asked about the developments on Wednesday, too, and wanted nothing to do with it.

"In no planet am I touching that," Kiffin said, via Michael Bratton of "That SEC Podcast."

Clearly, this legal battle between LSU and the SEC is far from over. LSU has attempted to have it dismissed, but the SEC has claimed that attempts to resolve it privately have failed.

Whether Luis actually sees the court with the Tigers, however, remains to be seen.

Later on Wednesday afternoon, the Georiga attorney general got involved and slammed LSU in a letter to SEC commissioner Greg Sankey.

Attorney General Christopher Carr called LSU out for a "pattern of destructive behavior," and encouraged the league to sanction LSU — "up to and including expulsion" from the league completely.

"Put simply, LSU is again attempting to benefit from the legal chaos it helped to coordinate and encourage," Carr wrote, via ESPN . "LSU's continued contempt for the rules of the SEC — rules they have voted on and agreed to — cannot go unaddressed.

This is the second such letter that Carr has written the SEC about LSU.

articles.title: Vanessa Bryant, Pau Gasol Reportedly Part of Ownership Group Attempting to Buy WNBA's Sparks
articles.summary: Hall of Famer Pau Gasol and Vanessa Bryant have shown interest in purchasing the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks, according to Tom Friend of Sports Business Journal.
articles.body:
Hall of Famer Pau Gasol and Vanessa Bryant have shown interest in purchasing the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks, according to Tom Friend of Sports Business Journal .

They're one of at least three prospective bidders. Another group is led by Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones, who recently purchased the MLB's San Diego Padres.

Bloomberg's Randall Williams, Sridhar Natarajan, and Lucas Shaw first reported in October that Mark Walter, having divested his stakes in the Los Angeles Lakers and Chelsea FC, is looking to sell the Sparks at a $700 million valuation.

Per Friend, the price tag "had initially been an issue for some prospective buyers." However, the sale will include the Sparks' standalone practice facility , and $700 million is less than where CNBC's Michael Ozanian valued the Golden State Valkyries ($1 billion).

Friend didn't rule out Josh Kushner and Bob Iger, who purchased the Lakers from Walter, from making a play for the Sparks, though they're unlikely to be the primary investors.

Gasol is already a minority shareholder in the WNBA. He contributed to the league's 2022 capital raise , which saw the league sell a 16 percent stake for $75 million.

Gasol and Bryant would also be familiar faces given their deep ties to the Lakers.

Broadly speaking, the fanbase will be eager to see an ownership change.

The Sparks have missed the playoffs for six straight seasons. Icons Candace Parker, Chelsea Gray and Nneka Ogwumike steadily left as free agents, though Ogwumike returned for her farewell season. General manager Raegan Pebley got the boot midway through the 2026 season, with head coach Lynne Roberts dismissed once the campaign concluded.

Since Los Angeles last reached the WNBA Finals in 2017, the team has been a chronic underperformer, and it doesn't have much to show after having pivoted to a rebuild a few years ago.

A new ownership regime may finally bring the stability the Sparks need to be a marquee franchise again.
